We employed an expansive statistical approach known as chemical cartography to analyze 10 elements in 136 stellar populations composed of 34182 stars observed across the Milky Way's disk. Using a two-component model, we identified distinct patterns in the stars' compositions, effectively reducing their data to 20 signals. By interpreting these signals, we learned that populations with higher metallicities and higher masses tend to exhibit larger alpha-enhancements, while others revealed insights into the stars' ages, distributions of radial locations, and surface rotations. Specific patterns, such as those related to the [Mg/Fe]-metallicity plane, highlighted the importance of rapid star formation in shaping chemical features. Similarly, others related to [Mn/Fe] and [Ni/Fe] suggested that elements produced by various nuclear reactions are sensitive to the properties of individual stellar populations. Moreover, chemical differences between populations of globular and field stars were also explored. By combining this study with a larger sample of APOGEE data, many previously observed features across the galaxy were confirmed, along with new ones, reinforcing the effectiveness of chemical cartography when using an expander dimensionality reduction technique.

During the COVID-19 pandemic in China, a wide array of rumors on social media has been observed, ranging from factual information and preventive measures to intrusive personal stories and unfounded survival claims. These diverse rumors have significant impact on public perception, policy implementation, and the overall progress of pandemic control. Despite the extensive research on online rumor dissemination, most studies have focused on specific topics such as financial, public health, and natural disasters, lacking comprehensive insights into the characteristics and dissemination patterns of rumors during the COVID-19 outbreak. This in turn hampers the applicability of existing models to future events. To address this gap, we analyze a substantial dataset comprising 2844 rumors,旨在深入探讨其特征及传播机制在疫情期间的特殊性。Our research reveals the distinctive content composition of rumors through unigrams and n-grams analysis, as well as the influential factors in their spread via feature importance assessment. Notably, our findings emphasize the notable role of official information dissemination in curbing rumor propagation. Based on these insights, we propose a novel two-stage model for evaluating the influence of rumors on individual posts, as demonstrated through visualization, statistical validation, and practical application.

The Fornax3D Consortium is establishing a comprehensive 3D map of the Fornax cluster's intermediate radius region, utilizing deep photometric and spectroscopic data to study the area's galaxy population. The consortium is focusing on identifying and analyzing nebulae, specifically nebular outflows and distortions, to gain insights into their dynamics and physical properties. These observations can aid in determining distances to galaxies through the expansion of their outflows along Hubble's law. The consortium aims to compile and distribute data sets regarding nebulae to the scientific community. Initially, they plan to present and analyze the characteristics of a sample of galaxy nebulae to demonstrate and test data processing methods to a wider audience. These methods, implemented through the use of the Fornax3D Pipeline, will enable researchers to automatically derive distances to galaxies based on their associated nebulae, utilizing an existing database of planetary nebulae as a guide.

Processing vast volumes of high-speed data is becoming ubiquitous across government, scientific, and commercial sectors. To handle this, stream processing systems provide the necessary framework for continuously analyzing data flows without interruption. However, conventional stream processing techniques struggle to efficiently utilize compute resources, as they execute analytics one record at a time, ignoring the similarities between consecutive data points that commonly occur. This inefficiency forces developers to compromise between performance and effective resource utilization. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel system called LifeFlow, which leverages the regularity of data to process streams in-batches, thereby improving runtime performance and stream processing capabilities. LifeFlow's design includes automatically adapting to changing data conditions and efficiently utilizing compute resources. Our evaluations highlight that LifeFlow offers up to 10x improved resource utilization and 6x reduced runtime for typical stream processing scenarios compared to existing systems, while also supporting complex operations impossible with existing stream processing systems.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in pointwise null curves, do not exist within time-orthogonal metrics in the context of differential geometry. Furthermore, we demonstrate that certain curves, such as those found in semi-Einstein, Einstein, and cosmological space-times, do not exist. Furthermore, we establish the conditions for a certain type of curve, known as the spiral of Bertrand, to exist within a 3-dimensional semi-Riemannian manifold and derive its mathematical formula. We also investigate the existence of this curve in specific cosmological space-times.

The development of classification models using deep neural networks has been widely successful, yet the optimal loss function to minimize during training remains relatively unexplored. Although the cross-entropy loss is commonly employed in research and practice, its prevalence stems more from tradition than empirical validation. This study undertakes a systematic examination of various loss functions commonly employed in classification tasks to identify which yields the best results. Our findings indicate that certain unconventional loss functions consistently outperform cross-entropy loss in specific applications, providing a notable, underutilized resource for practitioners.

A stabilizable boundary feedback controller for the Navier-Stokes equations is described, where the control gain matrix is constant and the control acts on a boundary section oriented at an angle. The proof of asymptotic stability relies on establishing a precise solution decay rate, supported by estimates of the control law's decay rate. Additionally, this work extends a previous finding from the Laplacian operator to the Navier-Stokes context. The arguments used are primarily based on abstract resolvent estimates and the generation of a strongly continuous semigroup of operators.

This research employs a comprehensive numerical modeling technique to analyze crystal formation processes caused by liquid polymer solidification. By utilizing the method introduced in associated literature, scientists can simulate this phenomenon taking into consideration the mechanical and thermal aspects of the developing crystals within the polymer material. The experimental setup involves a liquid styrene polymer which is subsequently subjected to thermal and mechanical stress through the application of two parallel plates. One of the plates is gradually cooled below the material's glass transition temperature, followed by sudden displacement of the upper plate to induce shear flow. The resulting microstructure development is analyzed through numerical simulation, which aligns well with the observed experimental outcomes. Furthermore, the modeling approach enables the investigation of the underlying causes of an observed asymmetry in the developing microstructure, revealing the material's viscoelastic properties to play a crucial role in this process.

When added magnetic fields, particularly those arising from spin, can cause a d-wave superconductor to lose its coherence, a triplet-state superconductor is formed. In the absence of the magnetic field, the newly formed time-reversal symmetry-broken superconductor exhibits condensed pairs in a triplet state, resembling the nematic phase. This research demonstrates that the condensed pairs' nematic property facilitates the separation of the spin and orbital degrees of freedom within the pairs. Consequently, the spin susceptibility rises abruptly at the transition to the triplet-state, as the spin is no longer in opposition to the magnetic field. This phenomenon provides a distinct signature that differentiates triplet nematic superconductivity from conventional triplet superconductivity. Furthermore, the theory of triplet nematic superconductivity enables the occurrence of Pauli paramagnetism, a phenomenon where the spin susceptibility becomes negative.

The availability of sensor data and constructed objects within computer-aided design formats, like STEP, can be leveraged to improve robotic skills through digital methods. This concept forms the basis of constructivistic meta-learning, a novel framework that uses feedback from virtual object interaction to translate it into sensory input for robotic learning. We define this conceptual framework and explore its application in the context of shape sorting using a 3D-printed interactive object and a robotic learner. The results of our experiments reveal significant advancements in sample efficiency and task generalization capabilities when incorporating this form of constructive feedback. Furthermore, the data supports a key finding – optimal object design does not always maximize performance.

Difference Carrier Phase (CPD) detection methods are typically associated with a 3-T symbol period delay, which varies for conventional differential detection. In contrast, our research demonstrates the feasibility of implementing differential detection schemes that incur a lower delay. Specifically, we develop novel differential detection methods for Continuous Phase Modulation (CPM) that are based on a 2-T symbol period, offering comparable performance to conventional methods. We prove the feasibility of these methods both theoretically and through simulation. In fact, we show that novel differential detection methods, which are based on a 2-T symbol period, perform better than conventional methods, which are based on a 3-T symbol period.

The process of a neutron star colliding with a black hole is still poorly understood due to limited observations, particularly in how the collision affects the neutron star's surface. This study proposes utilizing features of gravitational waves from the bounce of the neutron star to identify these events. We examine the relationship between the properties of the neutron star and the collision, discovering that the presence of a thermal signal depends on the star's mass-radius connection. This specific feature can reveal information about the equation of state, even in cases where the collision produces a disrupted spiral pattern or merges into a larger black hole. Consequently, combining observations from electromagnetic and multi-messenger messengers may provide valuable insights into the complex nature of these collisions.

Building on our previous investigation into the Quark-Gluon Plasma's quantum potential, our research has been expanded to the broader scenario of thermal thermal systems in a finite temperature range, exhibiting both thermal equilibrium and non-zero quantum potential. Utilizing a first-order approximation, we derived a comprehensive expression for thermal systems, allowing us to explore implications regarding thermal equilibrium, quantum stability, and the thermal variability of quantum potential. Furthermore, we studied how these aspects are influenced by thermal compressibility of spacetime, as well as its non-increasing counterpart, in the specified temperature range. Notably, we discovered that quantum potential varies in direct proportion to temperature, alongside demonstrating how thermal equilibrium, non-zero stability, and thermal compressibility of spacetime shape the representation of the quantum state within this finite temperature range.

The Disentangled Genetic Action Network (dGAN) addresses two simultaneous challenges in rain removal and image synthesis by decoupling rain formation and action into separate components.  During training, dGAN uses distinct latent spaces to capture the elements of rain, including its droplets, streaks, intensity, and orientation.  This allows dGAN to perform targeted actions on individual rain elements while simultaneously removing others.  For scenes without rain, combining rain formation and action modules enables dGAN to generate rainy conditions.  As a result, dGAN excels in rain elimination, synthesis, and creating simulated rainy environments from clear images.  The model was tested on the SPWR dataset, where its performance matched or surpassed the leading benchmarks in all three areas.

The widespread adoption of cluster-based rewards has outgrown the limitations of manually labeled examples, giving way to automatic methods for cluster validation and ranking. To investigate the feasibility of an interactive, visually guided ranking process, this study proposes a group-based interface that efficiently selects a few highly ranked subclusters from each group, thereby reducing the burden of annotation while maintaining its effectiveness. A comparative analysis with other active learning strategies and inertial benchmarks for both linear models and neural networks demonstrates the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its feasibility through our findings.

The failure of category theory frameworks to adequately depict topological and algebraic continuous functions stems from their reliance on set theory. This shortcoming isn't inherent to category theory, but rather a consequence of the specific framework's reliance on sets. By redefining the underlying concepts of size, we can create a new topological framework that preserves continuity without falling into the traditional pitfalls. This approach yields a striking result: the impossible continuum equation, $2^{|A|} = |Top(1,A)|$, holds true in this new framework.

We discuss the potential Q-curvature type problem within a bounded section of n-dimensional Euclidean space, specifically when n is 24 or greater and the section is defined by being less than a distance of 1 from the origin. A necessary and sufficient condition is established for conformal equivalent metrics within this bounded section to maintain a constant curvature in Q, mirroring previous findings that provided limit dimensions and ground state characteristics for associated restriction problems. Notably, our research highlights that constant Q curvature is achievable under such conditions within the 23-dimensional Euclidean space.

We introduce ATOMIC, a comprehensive resource for if-then inference in artificial intelligence, consisting of a structured database containing 12,000 descriptions of everyday objects, scenarios, and human interactions across various domains. ATOMIC is designed to serve as a foundation for pre-trained models that can reason in accordance with the world's common knowledge and can be utilized for tasks such as image classification, captioning, and visual question answering. Demonstrating the potential of if-then inference in everyday life, models trained on ATOMIC have significantly surpassing previous state-of-the-art results in multiple benchmark evaluations.

New, noisy quantum computers will face significant limitations in the accuracy of input data, especially in scenarios involving massive datasets typical of optimization tasks like portfolio selection. For instance, applying a quantum algorithm, such as HHL, to such scenarios will inherently depend on approximation of the input matrix condition number, which can be influenced by data inaccuracies. This research explores various implementations of the HHL algorithm that are conditioned by resource constraints and evaluates them for their robustness against these limitations. The results indicate that certain variations of the HHL algorithm, under certain conditions, can produce accurate solutions for certain types of linear systems, but may struggle with others. For portfolio selection, simulation tests comparing classical and quantum approaches, including an optimized classical version and the HHL algorithm, are conducted. The outcomes for portfolio performance, considering stability and asset selection aspects, are analyzed.

To improve multi-modal learning, a novel cross-modal attention mechanism called Speech-text Driven (S2T) and (T2S) Bidirectional Focus (T2S) is introduced. These models automatically emphasize the complementary relationship between modalities by incorporating speech and text attention networks into the training process. The proposed framework extends a current search engine helper system that uses both speech and text inputs, making it easier to interpret user queries through a combination of modalities. Furthermore, the model's ability to transfer knowledge and its S2T component are investigated. The results indicate that the proposed model significantly outperforms a unimodal baseline and a simple fusion approach, thanks to its speech and text attention networks that utilize modality-complementary information and its transfer learning capabilities. Driven by the need to overcome data sparsity issues, an open-source dataset called MS-RWA is released, which links speech search engine logs to text-based web search logs, even for cases where the speech query corresponds to an unobserved text query. The experiments indicate that incorporating this rich, bidirectional information during training refines the attention mechanism and boosts performance, particularly for models with transfer learning capabilities.

This research investigates a specific property of plane curves and a determinantal formula that expresses it. The formula involves the curve's curvature, mean curvature, and standard area element. The integral of this formula over a defined area bounded by the curve is constant and proportional to the curve's length. The theorem is then applied to specialized curves such as spirals of Archimedes, logarithmic spirals, and elliptical curves. Furthermore, parametric equations for curves that maintain constant values of this formula are generated using a new method and a specific class of these curves are obtained.

This paper precisely determines the average, variance, and entire probability distribution function for the highest initial value in a sequence of uniformly random parking functions, as well as any sequence containing it. We also establish that these initial values, when normalized, converge in distribution to the GUE Tracy-Widom distribution as the given parameters increase within the range of 2 to n-1. Furthermore, we derive precise formulas for the expected value and variance of the longest initial sequence of numbers that share a specific remainder when divided by n.

The superconducting transition in nanowires can be significantly impacted by a gate electrode, inducing a critical transition point. While the precise mechanism behind this phenomenon remains unclear in some materials, particularly metallic or weakly superconducting nanowires, this phenomenon has previously been attributed to coherent quantum interference or the Josephson effect in certain contexts. In a recent experiment involving nanowires with superconducting properties similar to NbN, the coincidence of this phenomenon with a 4e^2/h conductance peak led to the proposition of a new hybrid effect known as the IEC peak. However, an in-depth theoretical analysis revealed that an alternative, viable explanation lies in the resolution of a Coulomb blockade within the normal state of the device, effectively ruling out quantum interference as the primary mechanism. This finding suggests a more detailed examination of Discrete Charge Tunneling in superconducting tunnel junctions is required.

The red dwarf star GJ 229 was found to be accompanied by a tiny planet, GJ 229b, the initial discovered terrestrial-world or minor planet, the nature of which remains unclear.  With the planet/world exhibiting significantly higher temperatures, around 750K, research has revealed numerous spectral features on GJ 229b, yet significant ambiguity persists regarding its classification due to previous analysis methods lacking in accuracy.  By applying a precise and highly adaptable spectral line analysis to GJ 229b, we have established a more precise spectral profile, with a temperature of approximately 716K, a gas rotation rate of 12 km/s, and a reduced CO molecular abundance by a factor of 3.  With this new and more accurate spectral profile, we have established a list of top molecular targets for future study of GJ 229b.  With a estimated mass of around 3-4 times the mass of a planet, GJ 229b, with a relatively cool surface temperature, exhibits a rich spectrum with multiple molecular signatures.  With a gas rotation rate higher than expected, it's possible that significant vertical movement within the atmosphere of GJ 229b may be occurring.  With this precise spectral line analysis, we have established a detailed model of the atmosphere of GJ 229b, with a albedo of approximately 15-20

Studies in relativistic heavy-ion collisions indicate that the quark-gluon fluid is profoundly opaque, suggesting that inelastic scattering events between its components are extensive.  We demonstrate the impact of this characteristic on the evolution of such collisions, comparing theoretical models where inelastic scatters are either limited or unlimited in range.  Our results reveal that the so-called 'Moyen regime', achieved when scattering events are sufficiently extensive, has distinct, density-dependent characteristics that contrast with the outcomes of less intense scattering, especially regarding energy density and volume changes.  However, predicted differences in observable results from nuclear interaction experiments are minimal due to extensive multiple scattering, regardless of the quark-gluon fluid's opacity.

Predicting future video changes is particularly difficult due to its asymmetric nature. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that employs a dual representation, combining an explicit part with an implicit latent vector in a shared space. By utilizing a diverse set of 12 motion patterns from the ChangeNet dataset, our method effectively captures the complexity of the problem. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements, yielding the best existing results on benchmark datasets in both global and local metrics. Furthermore, our method is versatile and can be applied to various downstream tasks, including but not limited to action recognition and classification.

Valence electron dynamics within multi-electron atoms can be effectively studied
through time-resolved x-ray experiments, offering insights into the interaction
between adjacent orbital electrons. Such  atomic systems serve as foundational
to understanding complex, light-excited solid materials with correlated electrons.
In this study, magnesium excited by extreme ultraviolet light exhibits inter-orbital
electron interaction across the 2s and 2p orbits. By measuring spectroscopic
parameters, specifically the 2s-2p splitting energy, over time post-excitation,
we observe a delayed  s-band electron transition induced by a core core shaking
process following light exposure.  In contrast to more complex systems with
electrons distributed across multiple shells, electrons within a single shell,
such as this system, provide an easily interpretable model, facilitating deeper
analysis of light induced electron correlations within solid materials.

The Ω-baryon, which contains two s-quarks and one non-strange quark, has a direct
experimental avenue for investigation through spectroscopic analysis using
SPC (Single Particle Capture).  A high-rate experiment at J-PARC with a 110
GeV/m2 beam intensity has been conducted to gather data on resonance
production via the single-K capture method.  These measurements resulted in
an 18 times improvement in signal-to-noise ratio, notably enhancing the
evidence for the Ω-baryon and its excited states, such as the $\Omega(2129)$,
relative to previous reports.  To better understand the dynamics of this system,
we employed both global and local statistical models to analyze the mass
spectrum with an emphasis on end-point parameters.  Our refined calculations
demonstrate statistically significant (at the 3$\sigma$ level or higher)
agreement with established mass values for ground and excited state hadro-$\Lambda_{c}^{+}$
baryons, as well as the ground state strange $\bar{\Omega}^{+}$ baryon.

Predicting how rapidly infectious diseases spread through a population is an especially challenging problem when considering urban settings with high person-to-person contact rates and high mobility.  To tackle this complex issue, we have developed a novel data collection and processing system that provides high-quality data on face-to-face interactions occurring on city buses.  Since its deployment in Tucson, Arizona during the 2020-2021 flu season, this system has gathered multiple data sets containing various features that reflect overall contact intensity, spatial distribution, and connectivity.  By plugging in appropriate parameters, researchers are now able to make accurate predictions about contact intensity based on local COVID-19 case counts.  Our results demonstrate the power of high-quality data in providing reliable estimates of contact intensity, as well as informed assumptions in the absence of direct measurements.  We have also ranked several machine learning models to identify the most effective method for contact intensity estimation, while accounting for data noise and missing values.  Our findings also highlight the most accurate model for this task - linear regression with imputed short-cut edges.  Ultimately, this system not only facilitates the study of disease spread on public transit but also on private vehicles, as we show through preliminary analysis of data collected in Scottsdale, Arizona during the same time period.

Quantum electrodynamics predicts subtle effects in the quantum vacuum such as light scattering and the splitting of polarized light during the diffraction processes, which are technically difficult to detect due to their minuscule magnitudes. This difficulty has historically confined research on how the quantum vacuum influences photon behavior to highly controlled experiments. However, recent breakthroughs have demonstrated that utilizing crystal diffraction can significantly amplify the QED vacuum polarization splitting, making it detectable. These findings suggest that conventional diffraction processes, such as that found in standard grating devices, could also showcase measurable QED vacuum polarization effects on photons.

This note presents an updated and more accessible version of the algorithm originally devised by Eisenlohr and Farris for determining complete transitivity in point sets within a plane, a solid space, or their n-dimensional analogs. Their initial formulation was complicated due to an error in reference, which this revision corrects and clarifies.

Physical layer security is an emerging keyless authentication method gaining
interest in its capability to securely verify the authenticity of a transmission
without requiring pre-shared secrets. Although research in this field has been
conducted for Gaussian noise channels, the necessity of employing sophisticated
channel estimation techniques has limited its practical application. This study
demonstrates a novel approach to achieving secure verification in noise-based
channels, thus providing a framework for studying this concept in more complex
channel environments. The proposed method involves the creation of a statistical
test, which serves as both the verification process and extraction technique. This
method is analytically characterized for Gaussian noise channels and experiments
demonstrate its robustness to channel estimation errors. The method's performance
is evaluated through theoretical analysis and experimental results, highlighting
its limitations and potential for enhancement through sophisticated techniques
such as optimum test design and matched filtering.

We investigate the possibility of flat-band surface plasmons (FBSPs) in twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMTMDCs), which consist of two different TMD monolayers. Using the su(3) tight-binding plus RPA methodology, we demonstrate that a distinct FBSP mode arises from twisted valleys within the moiré superlattice. This internal FBSP is highly robust, exhibiting low damping and large confinement, with a linewidth as small as 3.4 meV and a confinement factor close to 100 at 5% filling. Notably, internal FBSPs are prevalent in various TMTMDC combinations, in contrast to same-material twisted bilayer TMDs, where external FBSPs are more common. These internal FBSPs are ideal for applications such as light detection, feedback systems, and low-loss feedback loops due to their low sensitivity to the environment and high confinement,同时还具备高度可调的平带特性。

This research paper extends the analysis of gradient Ricci solitons within the domain of Sasakian manifolds. We have specifically investigated conformal Ricci solitons within this context and established a new formula for the Ricci curvature of a gradient Ricci soliton in a Sasakian manifold. Additionally, we have demonstrated that in a 3-dimensional conformal Ricci soliton within this type of manifold, the potential function is an eigenfunction of the Laplacian operator with an eigenvalue of 2. Furthermore, we have obtained a metric for a Ricci soliton within a Kenmotsu manifold and identified that such solitons are never steady and always expanding.

This review of stellar winds and magnetic fields in stars, as well as in planets, moons, and other celestial bodies, synthesizes the processes governing these phenomena. We examine how stellar activity drives winds and magnetic fields in stars, and subsequently, how planetary systems subjected to these influences develop their own wind-magnetosphere interactions. This review also compares these processes to those occurring within the Earth's magnetosphere. Additionally, we explore the potential for atmospheric loss in planetary systems as a consequence of this interaction. A particular focus is given to solar activity during the Maunder Minimum and its impact on Earth's magnetosphere, as well as on Mars and Mars' atmosphere. We contrast these interactions with observations of Mars today and how atmospheric escape mechanisms differ between the two scenarios. Finally, we discuss these processes in the context of ancient Mars, the current atmosphere of the gas giant Jupiter, and the emerging atmosphere of Saturn's moon Titan.

Spin-orbit proximity effects result from strong interactions at the interface between heavy-element materials and ferromagnets, yielding significant spin-orbit coupling within the ferromagnetic layer and modifying its magnetic properties. This research focuses on examining the spin-orbit proximity effect in M/BI2SE (M=Pt, PB) multilayer systems, leveraging Intercalated Lu-Si doped B and Intercalated Pb-doped B materials, to analyze spin-orbit coupling modification and energy band modification. By adjusting the thickness of the BI2SE/Plb layer and analyzing magnetic hysteresis loop and skewness in the Intercalated Lu-Si doped B/Plb multilayer systems, researchers can distinguish between magnetic anisotropy and spin-orbit coupling. The occurrence of magnetic skewness indicates localized magnetic anisotropy, while magnetic hysteresis indicates the preservation of magnetic skewness due to strong magnetic anisotropy. Furthermore, the absence of magnetic skewness indicates magnetic anisotropy localization within the BI2SE/Plb multilayer systems, with the systems exhibiting bi-linear or tri-linear magnetic hysteresis depending on the Bi/Pb concentration. This research provides an in-depth understanding of the spin-orbit proximity effect, adjusting bi-linear magnetic anisotropy into tri-linear magnetic anisotropy, and facilitating the discovery of exotic phase transitions such as tri-state quantum phase and tri-critical quantum phase

This study presents analytical solutions to the fractional Schrödinger equation, utilizing the generalized Mie-type potential in higher dimensions. Employing Jumarie type fractional derivative, the parameter space is reduced, and the problem is transformed into an equivalent form. The analysis incorporates a non-local operator to derive solutions in their original context. Validity of obtained solutions is verified through application of Laplace transform, alternative method. Furthermore, graphical representations are generated for a various selection of parameters in the fractional domain.

We introduce a novel perspective on training neural networks through consistency. Specifically, we focus on the sensitivity of network outputs to input changes and incorporate a consistency criterion to guide the network's robustness. This approach amounts to imposing a limit on the Lipschitz constant of the neural network. We demonstrate that an optimal neural network configuration can be found by applying penalty methods and, under certain conditions, equivalent formulations are possible using network controllers or augmented loss functions. A key finding is that penalizing the neural network's Laplacian norm achieves Lipschitz consistency, paving the way for efficient optimization through local approximations. We propose an alternative method to traditional optimization techniques, introducing a regularized minimax problem for mean squared error. This leads to a new approach to training neural networks, involving the penalty method. We derive the equivalent conditions for optimal configurations and propose an efficient optimization strategy. We validate our method's performance through numerical experiments.

The views of partners in a relationship often evolve in response to one another,
 ultimately leading to a unified perspective. This phenomenon is Oneward Consensus.
 Recent research suggests that Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models can successfully
 replicate the OWC phenomenon within a social context. However, existing studies are
 limited by their focus on the parameters of the model, using a uniform learning rate
 for all participants. A more realistic scenario would involve two agents with varying
 update rules within a social dilemma scenario, specifically the Prisoner's Dilemma.
 We investigated the LSTM's ability to capture OWC within this scenario by studying
 its performance in a PD game played by two agents with opposite preferences.
 We found that the LSTM fails to replicate the consensus effect due to its symmetrical
 design. To address this limitation, we introduced an asymmetrical version of the LSTM,
 and found that it could accurately reproduce the consensus effect, but only when the
 model was not over-trained. As training progressed, the consensus effect gave way to
 an anti-consensus effect, where the agents adopted the view of the leader. Interestingly,
 adding a slight advantage to the model in terms of payoffs, could enhance both OWC and
 ACW. These effects were also observed when using a traditional multi-layer perceptron,
 highlighting the importance of the architectural design of the model.

Recent observations of the planet HD 80606 b, which will soon be targeted by the James Webb Space Telescope, offer a unique opportunity to study its thermal emissions and potential atmosphere via a combination of ground-based and space-based tools. To maximize these observations, especially during the planet's highly eccentric orbit, we have conducted a thorough eclipse time analysis using data from a global network of telescopes. By comparing the observed and predicted eclipse times, we have been able to refine the planet's orbital parameters and improve the effectiveness of observation scheduling with the James Webb Space Telescope. Our results indicate that HD 80606 b is on a closed orbit without significant influence from other stars, and the deviation from the predicted eclipse times is now known to be within the margin of error. Furthermore, we have proposed new observation schedules that would increase the chance of syncing with the telescope's schedule.

Video games have significantly contributed to rehabilitation therapies over the past few decades and have been incorporated into the development of assistive technologies for movement and mobility. This work offers an overview of existing frameworks that combine robotic gameplay with rehabilitation and assistive technology, highlighting how these frameworks have been utilized in these fields. The document discusses three representative frameworks for physically interactive gaming: robotic sports, penalty kicks, and soccer, which have potential applications in helping individuals with mobility impairments regain movement and muscle strength. The document also explores potential future enhancements to these frameworks, such as integrated tracking systems, virtual reality, and artificial intelligence.

We derive the variational convergence of certain functionals under piecewise-linear approximations with increasing density, following Γ-convergence principles, under both continuous and discrete settings. This framework encompasses specific convex regularisation functionals, such as total variation and brittle fracture models, specifically Branching Phase Field (BPF) functional. By analysing the discrete Γ-convergence of these piecewise-linear approximations, we establish an approximate representation of the limit functional for a particular class of inputs. This representation enables us to establish strong approximations of the BPF functional by employing piecewise-linear mappings.

Deep neural networks have significantly reduced noise in low-dose PET images by training on moderate-dose data, but their performance degrades with significantly lower doses due to limited synthetic low-dose training data. To address this issue, we introduce a new approach called Multimodal Conscious Transfer Learning (MultiCoT) that leverages not only normal probability distributions of high-dose data but also outlier distributions, as contained in count-synthesized low-dose data with extended tails, to enable the model to handle reduced-dose PET images outside of its training data. Specifically, MultiCoT utilizes count-synthesized ultra-low-dose PET data to update the predictive variance of a previously trained model on moderate-dose data, making use of a transferable transformation to preserve the outcome of the original model's prediction. Furthermore, we introduce an extended training framework outside of Normal distributions for Mean and Variance networks, allowing them to learn from count-synthesized ultra-low-dose PET images, thereby improving the model's ability to handle significantly lower doses. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our proposed method outside of Normal (MultiCoT-O) outperforms existing reduced-dose PET reconstruction techniques at very low doses, particularly at 1/50th of a normal dose, and is capable of handling even more reduced doses.

Multi-tenant SaaS systems, despite providing rapid and cost-effective software, often fall short in accommodating tenant-specific requirements due to their highly standardized nature. To address this limitation, we suggest a flexible, tenant-personalized approach that allows for the discreet modification of application code within each tenant's specific context. Our method incorporates a customizable layer built on top of Node.js applications, enabling unique code deployment, automatic data security translation, and seamless integration with existing frameworks like Mocha, Express.js, and Node.js. Key features of our approach include a modular architecture, an established API for seamless functionality, and robust security measures, ultimately ensuring each tenant's data remains secure, their specific needs met, and their system performance uncompromised.

The concept of centering, originally proposed by Grimes and later expanded by Chafe, suggests that the most recent mention in a conversation or text will typically be repeated in the following sentence or section. This theory has been frequently discussed but rarely empirically supported. To investigate its validity, this study analyzed the co-occurrence rates of noun phrase (NP) mentions in the Facebook caption corpus, utilizing both a rule-based and a neural approach to coreference resolution. Our analysis revealed a significant increase in the head-to-another centering strategy from the random baseline to the actual data. Furthermore, the neural system outperformed the centering-based rule-based system, suggesting that learned representations may encode information relevant to noun phrase co-occurrence, potentially centering tendencies included. To further examine this, we developed a centering-based rule that mirrored the performance of the neural system.

In this study, we explore the parametric complexity of several parameterized problems related to upward planarity. Specifically, we identify the parameterized complexity of deciding binary upward outerplanarity for general graphs, and those with series-parallel structure, providing both a linear-time algorithm and an XP algorithm for general graphs. We also reveal that recognizing binary upward tree-partitions falls under the constant-time category for planar graphs, and is solvable in linear time for graphs with fixed treewidth. Additionally, we establish that recognizing binary upward tree-partitions is NP-complete for graphs with bounded pathwidth. Finally, we discover that determining whether a graph admits an upward embedding as a partial subgraph is equivalent to recognizing binary upward tree-partitions.

Customized evaluation frameworks are commonly employed to assess new NLP techniques relative to established benchmarks, nevertheless, the process of creating a new one is frequently manual and time-consuming. We have developed a new system called Autoframework, which is designed to automate the creation of evaluation frameworks. It achieves this by using pre-built components to automate account setup, environment configuration, benchmark replication, and evaluation protocols. We have demonstrated the effectiveness of our system by automatically developing multiple evaluation frameworks for models involving dialog state tracking, model distillation in the context of conversational interfaces, and multi-task learning for natural language understanding.

Using location-based services relies heavily on determining where individuals are. Traditionally, methods to achieve this involve GPS, beacon technology, or WiFi. Each approach comes with its own set of limitations and drawbacks. Our proposed solution utilizes a combination of Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques to create a new approach for range assessment based on WiFi signals. This method, which we call DeepFRA, forecasts the distance between signal source and receiver by utilizing features automatically learned from lower-level layers of neural networks to output results in continuous numerical values. Preliminary findings using DeepFRA demonstrate the potential of combining advanced learning techniques for range assessment, achieving a mean estimation error of approximately 0.8 meters in indoor settings.

An alternative theory to dark matter, often referred to as modified gravity, suggests that matter's response to gravity changes at certain scales, potentially explaining some phenomena usually attributed to dark matter. In a specific case, the theory known as Big Bang Relativistic Gravity (BBRG) predicts that large, dense objects like neutron stars could be surrounded by a self-generated 'Dyson Shell' due to the recurrence of scattering processes within a specific scattering range. This occurs without any additional pressure to balance forces within the system, instead, the systems reach equilibrium at discrete states. Calculations indicate that for certain types of BBRG, a Dyson Shell could stabilize against gravitational collapse for massive stars, although it would not protect them from evaporation. Over time, these massive stars would lose mass, causing their scattering range to shrink and eventually become smaller than required for the formation of a Dyson Shell. As the BBRG models that support Dyson Shells do allow for radiation from within their systems, some characteristics of these stars should be observable.

Network-pooled expertise (NPE) technology enables multiple parties to take advantage of each other's resources over local networks. This study leverages NPE to develop a distributed method of detecting when service level agreements (SLAs) are being violated. As organizations increasingly rely on service level agreements to govern the performance of their internal and external services, there is a growing need for automatic systems that can identify when an SLA is being breached. By utilizing the collaborative power of NPE, the proposed approach offers a method of detecting SLA violations in a distributed manner. This study presents a framework for this collaborative detection system and outlines its operation through simulation results. The results indicate that this method can pinpoint the source of SLA violations and locate the affected service within a network. Additionally, the proposed system has the capability to pinpoint both the identifier and location of an SLA breach simultaneously. The results also demonstrate that this system is capable of doing so with minimal additional computational power, with only a small increase in detection accuracy compared to a single-source system, with NPE enabling the task to be achieved with up to 1.5 times less available expertise.

Beam fragmentation instability poses a significant challenge to regenerative beam extraction in energy recovery linacs and is primarily caused by vacuum chamber geometry and beam configuration. This issue is也很难 to control due to its sensitive dependence on beam parameters such as current distribution. In order to overcome this limitation, an alternative method is proposed by introducing a periodic perturbation rather than a regenerative beam extraction, which has been theoretically analyzed and numerically validated. The proposed method significantly reduces the beam fragmentation sensitivity to beam configuration, primarily favoring a loose meander beam configuration for optimal performance. The feasibility of this alternative method is demonstrated at a prototype energy recovery linac facility.

Integrating radiation sensors directly into neutron cross-section measurement targets is the next critical step in advancing the CITN methodology. To achieve this critical development phase, a 3D-scintillator sensor with 3-nanometer thickness has been designed and built to detect individual neutrons with minimal 1.4-millimeter angular resolution while causing negligible target perturbation due to its low atomic number and thin structure. By combining high-rate capability, high spatial resolution, and three-dimensional tracking capabilities, this novel sensor technology is set to overcome previous limitations and enable more precise and efficient measurements. A simulation of the neutron measurement process with this innovative sensor has been conducted, yielding a achievable resolution of 2.5 percent at a 10-kiloelectron-barn neutron energy of 207 megaelectron volts with a 10-microsecond measurement duration, which can be optimized for even better results.

In order to study this, we examine the light that escapes from dust as it releases trapped light and how this affects the clumping together of dust, and we find that warm dust is not as able to clump together and form larger structures as cold dust, and we explore various factors that may be influencing this, and we find that the ability of dust to clump together and form larger structures is not as affected by the ability of dust to clump together and form larger structures is not affected by the ability of dust to clump together and form larger structures, and we find that the ability of dust to clump together and form larger structures, and we find that the ability of dust to clump together and form larger structures, and we find that the ability of dust to

The Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis (LFD) method, a local variation of the Fisher method, addresses the limitation of the original method that relied on linear assumptions. While the Fisher method is well-established in its linear form for image classification, it has limited effectiveness in complex, high-dimensional cases. LFD extends this by leveraging local data structures to provide a more detailed examination within low-dimensional spaces. Our new R package enables LFD analysis, including an examination of the Hessian matrix's eigenvalues and uses both LFD and FA to generate an enhanced scatter plot loader.

To replicate the skills of human operators who employ rigid tools to manipulate objects in a confined space, we developed a new imitation learning method that accounts for nonlinear rigid constraints and barrier evading. This method is part of the broader EKMP framework, which collects data from two sources: free motion and restricted motion evading barriers. By selecting motion trials that avoid barriers from the collected data, our approach uses a kernel technique to identify subspaces in which the collection of free and barrier-evading data overlap, effectively reducing the dimensionality of the collection. As a result, the method enables the operator to use a variety of rigid tools to manipulate objects, as long as the collection of subspaces they impose overlaps with the obstacle. Moreover, the method ensures smooth object motion by increasing the barrier evading data's weight. Experiments with a two-link robot and a four-degree-of-freeryt hand-held device have shown the method's robust performance, with successful imitation of operators using different tools and devices.

To access two-loop form-factor and amplitude relations in N^4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, a critical dependency on the precise known central-emission vertex for gluons rests. Until now, this key element has been inferred from higher-order data, but as a direct calculation has yet to be undertaken. In this study, we undertake a direct one-loop determination of this elusive vertex. Furthermore, it provides a foundational step towards establishing the two-loop central-emission vertex.

Within the Rashba Hubbard model with near-nodal Rashba spin-orbit coupling and moderate on-site attraction, we have found that superfluidity can emerge as an insulator in a spin-singlet topological superfluid (TOSL) phase. By increasing the spin-orbit coupling, the TOSL phase is found to be isolated between two trivial insulator (IS) phases, with both IS phases occurring on opposing sides of a non-trivial Toric Code Mott insulator (MIM). Notably, the boundary between the two trivial insulator phases is a direct result of a topological phase transition within the Toric Code MIM. Utilizing the Hubbard-U framework, we have identified a regime where the TOSL exists between two trivial insulator phases at high Hubbard-U limits. Literature suggests that superfluidity can manifest as a Toric Code MIM in the Rashba Hubbard framework with moderate on-site attraction with near-nodal spin-orbit coupling, which is consistent with the results of a large-N mean-field theory analysis. Furthermore, this analysis also suggests that the TOSL can be elevated to a higher-order Toric Code TOSL (hTOSL) by increasing the spin-orbit coupling, with both sides of the hTOSL boundary exhibiting the same trivial insulator phase. Interestingly, this boundary distinguishes between two distinct trivial insulator phases that possess the same Chern number.

In certain cuprate superconductors, another type of quantum state competition with superconductivity is characterized by a non-symmetrical order that hinders the flow of electrons without resistance. Our analysis of resistivity and resistive transition data in YBCO reveals a unique quantum state with this electron pair character, which appears at an temperature of 63K. By using vortex liquids as an analogy for gaseous states, we found that this electron pair state may be associated with a square lattice of vortices, occurring at varying magnetic fields and temperatures within the superconducting phase diagram.

The behavior of fluid polymer brushes has significant implications for the operation of micro- and nanoscale pneumatic actuators and pumps, yet previous research on disordered polymer brush regions excluded certain highly elongated configurations. We develop a comprehensive Monte Carlo simulation that fills this knowledge gap by modeling disordered polymer brush regions in any shape. Our Monte Carlo simulation also enables us to derive stochastic differential equations describing polymer brush surface dynamics, based on finite sample approximations. Monte Carlo simulations and the derived equations both validate each other and provide predictions regarding the movement of polymer brush interfaces, design speeds that minimize surface noise, and the power consumed by surface noise. Our research directly provides the power consumption formula, addressing a long-standing issue in the study of brush actuators. We validate our findings through experimental measurements of designed polymer brush structures, utilizing high-speed microscopy.

A graph G is considered resolvable by a set S if every vertex in G can be uniquely identified by the distance information from the elements in S. This concept was first introduced by Slater in 1977 and later expanded upon by Harary and Wilf in the same year. A subset R of S is now referred to as a shortened metric generator if all vertices in G can be partially resolved using it. The minimum size of such subsets is defined as the shortened metric dimension of G and denoted by \tilde{\beta}(G). In this paper, we investigate the properties of \tilde{\beta}(G) for various types of graphs, including cycles, star graphs, and their products. We also establish a relationship between the shortened metric dimension of graphs and their binary representations. Furthermore, we prove that for any graph G, the shortened metric dimension is less than or equal to the metric dimension and the sum of the degree of freedom and the number of edge disjoint cycles.

Recent research utilizing high-resolution images from the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope has drawn significant interest in gamma-ray astrophysics. These images simulate various phenomena by combining simulations with real observational data. A key aspect of this study involves classifying sources that vary in intensity. We examine the performance of different machine learning techniques for analyzing time-series data from these sources. Specifically, we evaluate their effectiveness in distinguishing between sources that fluctuate in brightness and those that remain steady. Our findings indicate that algorithms such as Random Forest and XGBoost can accurately model global patterns based on observations and highlight variable sources using a classification approach using time-series data with a accuracy of about 95%.

A recent study examining voting systems concluded that no method exists to improve upon the serial dictatorship system while maintaining equivalence. However, we have developed an order in which alternatives can be considered, demonstrating that the serial dictatorship system is not the most efficient order. Furthermore, we have established that while there is not a single most optimal sequence, there are actually infinitely many sequences that are at least as desirable as the serial dictatorship sequence.

We analyzed 72 main-belt asteroids from the Pan-STARRS1 survey, specifically 40 of them in detailed study. The researchers selected these asteroids based on their visual absolute magnitudes and rotation periods, later expanding the sample to 400 asteroids with specific criteria on their visual absolute magnitudes. They conducted shape model analyses on the asteroids by studying their photometric light curves, identifying 34 binary asteroids, 16 of which are newly discovered. The ratio of binary to total asteroids in the detailed study was found to be 11 percent, but it rises to an estimated 4.9 percent in the larger field based on their errors estimates. The binary asteroids exhibit rotation periods between 0.56 to 4.9 hours and their secondary asteroids are generally less than 0.4 times the diameter of their primary counterparts. The discovery rate of binary asteroids appears to be rising with increasing asteroid diameter.

This research introduces a novel, flexible regression model that combines linear and non-linear components, known as the partially linear regression framework. The study derives estimates for the model's parameters, establishing statistical convergence rates under specific assumptions. A novel algorithm is then developed to solve the complex, high-dimensional non-linear aspects of the model. A simulation experiment is designed to evaluate the accuracy and efficiency of the estimates across various scenarios. Finally, a method is proposed to analyze peer influences within networks using this framework, with theoretical derivations extending the existing understanding of partial peer influence models.

This study introduces novel formulations for the Variable-Order Riemann-Liouville Variable-Order Integral and Derivative Operator, building on a recently introduced concept. We derive key properties and establish novel connections for these new operators, along with an application to solve differential equations using the Variable-Order Riemann-Liouville Variable-Order Derivative.

Location estimation methods help determine the relative positions of objects or resources in various settings, including earthquake source detection and electronic device tracking. By analyzing random signals in a planned grid, we can evaluate the minimum error in locating these sources using statistical measures like mean squared error (MSE). Our study focuses on a coherent detection method using an least-squares approach, and we develop a way to optimally balance the algorithm's complexity with real-world performance. Through simulations and real-world experiments with multiple sources, we demonstrate how the chosen method can achieve near-optimal results while significantly reducing computation time.

We've developed an updated version of the visualization tools we've previously released for spectral and spatial data from compact telescopes. The new version, which is now available online, includes the addition of interactive graphics. Furthermore, we've made the tools capable of processing data in real-time.

The Southern Atlantic Ocean's opening began in the Jurassic period, initially forming along a shear zone in the southwestern缘 of the African plate's margin.  A shift in the plate margin to a normal fault zone occurred in the Cenozoic era.  This change caused the South American and African plates to move apart at varying rates and directions, significantly affecting the ocean floor's morphology, including its depth, magnetic anomalies, and seafloor spreading centers.  Experts believe that large-scale intraplate events, such as the Cameroon Volcanic Line and East African Rift, may have influenced the region's dynamics.  To clarify the complexity of this region, researchers used an advanced method called finite elements to recreate the movement of the South American and African plates over the past 65 million years.  Their study revealed multiple phases of plate interaction, characterized by different patterns of stress, strain, and neotectonic activity, during the Cenozoic era in detail.  Specifically, they observed the Cameroon East African Rift influenced the region's dynamics during the Miocene and Pliocene epochs, whereas the region's early Oligocene to mid-Miocene plate margin showed significant intraplate events with reduced connectivity between the two plates, according to their modeling results during the Cenozoic era.

In unsupervised image segmentation, limited annotation resources often hinder the development of accurate models. To mitigate this, boundary-conscious information optimization (BCIO) is proposed as a boundary-aware self-supervised learning method. BCIO leverages oriented random wavelets (ORW) to create distorted wavelet maps, which preserve boundary regions and allow for precise match scoring between distorted and original images. A wavelet match network is then trained to minimize the difference in match scores, effectively learning an orientation and scale invariant feature representation. When combined with a distance-based partition network, BCIO achieves robust medical image segmentation. Experiments on hepatic tumor segmentation demonstrate that this method outperforms existing self-supervised methods and rivals models trained with annotated data.

Automated testing ensures the accuracy of software systems by simulating various scenarios to identify potential flaws.
To enhance this process, the author proposes using machine learning to adaptively generate test cases that target specific areas of software and simulate real user behavior.
Building on this idea, the author suggests using a machine learning-based dungeon supervisor to guide a text-based adventure game, learning to communicate and achieve goals through game events.
To evaluate this approach, the author creates a custom machine learning module and two custom dungeons, one requiring the creation of a game item and another requiring a specific creature to be defeated for progress.
The results show that the author's proposed method outperforms random testing, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving software development processes.
The author's framework combines the benefits of game enjoyment and efficient testing, allowing players to focus on their characters' goals while producing high-quality test cases.
This concept of a dungeon supervisor can be applied to other text-based games, one programming education tool, and various software development processes, making it a versatile and valuable idea.

Current lexico-semantic resources, widely employed by translators, facilitate the identification of synonyms and antonyms in languages, but fall short in capturing instances where words change both in meaning and opposite polarity across languages. The lack of comprehensive, detailed, and consistent annotations of lexical semantics in existing bilingual resources negatively impacts the development of Lexical Change Detection (LCD) systems. This paper introduces a new, extensive, and meticulously annotated dataset of lexical semantic transformations within context across languages, comprising 10,355 instances of antonyms and 3,581 instances of synonyms that have reversed their polarity. We propose a baseline system for context-dependent lexical semantic transformation detection, leveraging contextual embeddings and initializing embeddings from a lexical resource, achieving an F-score of 0.8151 for distinguishing reversed polarity antonyms from reversed polarity synonyms in five-fold cross-validation.

We employ a Bessel function framework to analyze the transverse momentum dependence of (quasi)parton distribution functions, and derive analytical formulas for various mean $k_\perp$-dependent characteristics, including the second-order moment. Utilizing a fitting model, we derive (quasi)parton distribution functions and their corresponding characteristic equations for valence and sea quarks, as well as gluons, and analyze the $x$-dependent behavior of these characteristics. Our results reveal distinct patterns in how these characteristics vary, with some following similar trajectories to others while displaying complementary features. Notably, our study re-emphasizes the significance of incorporating transverse momentum dependence into (quasi)parton distribution research, a concept first introduced by Yuan and Provencher and further developed by other researchers.

Research into the three-dimensional structure of proteins has gained significant interest due to their biological functionality, particularly those containing intricate knots. Understanding the folding and folding pathways of knotted proteins presents a major challenge in this field. This study proposes using the concept of torsional rigidity to identify folding pathways in knotted proteins, focusing on preserving their intrinsic geometric properties. By applying this method, we identify distinct folding routes in DnaA and Cro proteins, avoiding unnecessary deviations caused by artificial surface adjustments. These identified pathways correspond to specific regions of the proteins responsible for forming knots, which may have relevance to their folding processes. Additionally, this research explores the potential of torsional rigidity in analyzing folding patterns in DNA.

By integrating Planck's 2018 data with the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Collaboration's 2015/2016 and 2017/2018 samples, researchers analyzed the Early Dark Energy model through a specific likelihood approach.
