This article provides $2$ distinct proof methodologies establishing the existence of pairs of relatively prime positive integers, $a$ and $b$, for which the expression $a^2+ab+b^2$ is divisible by $7^n$ for any given positive integer $n$. Notably, these proofs also establish that $a$ and $b$ remain relatively prime when raised to the power of $n$.

Mobile robots equipped with jumping mechanisms are highly effective in navigating loose and sinking terrains by swiftly exiting the terrain by jumping. To accurately predict and control these jumping robots' behavior, it is essential to consider the factors of damping and stiffness that affect their interaction with the terrain. By incorporating a spring-damper model into the analysis of vertical motion, this study develops a control strategy for a single-legged jumping robot to achieve optimal take-off performance. Furthermore, the study simulates the robot's behavior using this control model and compares its performance to that of a traditional spring-damper model.

Using a cohesive model, we employ the moment method to derive flexible parameterizations for the form factors and shape factors of mesons composed of quarks with non-zero masses. Specifically, our calculations account for the electromagnetic interactions of quarks, and we obtain consistent results for both form factors and shape factors. Notably, our model predicts a non-zero radius for scalar mesons, and we show that the relationships between the form factors of heavy quark pairs satisfy expectation in the heavy quark limit.

Historically, research into the droplet electrohydrodynamic fan has been confined to oil due to its high boiling point. We break this limitation in this study by successfully showcasing droplet EHD fan behavior with liquid aerosols, specifically alcohol. By analyzing and comparing the emission patterns of both alcohol and oil under varying voltages, we found significant differences. Alcohol emissions quickly attain a stable state in response to voltage increases, in contrast to oil emissions which exhibit a distinct lag. Furthermore, alcohol drops undergo rapid acceleration and acceleration after reaching a certain voltage threshold. Alcohol emissions also exhibit a higher sensitivity to voltage changes when near a certain point, as opposed to oil emissions which display a notable lag. Additionally, we investigated an anomaly where alcohol near a certain point undergoes a reduction in density in response to voltage increases.

Some sentences employ negation to convey a contrast between two opposing ideas, 
indicating that while one idea may seem unjustified, the other is justified. 
Understanding how negation functions within a textual context can be a challenging 
task for natural language processing systems. To examine and improve this 
particular aspect, we introduce CONDAQA, a new dataset comprising 440 examples 
of contrastive negation, consisting of pairs of questions drawn from existing 
datasets that rely on explicit factual information to derive reasonable answers. 
Through experiments, we show that current interpretation models struggle to 
grasp the negation-based reasoning within this dataset, thereby highlighting a 
gap in their capabilities. Furthermore, CONDAQA fills a gap in existing 
interpretation comprehension benchmarks by addressing the understanding of 
negation within textual contexts, particularly the contrastive aspect.

Our new approach, herearch+, builds upon the successful principles of herearch to not only classify large datasets but also preserve the integrity of current hierarchies as the dataset grows. We now support the incremental expansion of hierarchies, allowing for added categories, and can be seen on our web interface at https://herearchplus.org/.

We used Advanced Sounder for Initial Satellite Appraisal (IASI) radiometer data of the Earth's outgoing radiation and wind speed information from the Global Reanalysis for the Initial Condition and Predictions system (ERA5) to calculate the mean square width of the wave crests calculated by Cox and Munk. Their formula, a classic parameter for measuring the shape of water waves, was found to closely match our results in various ocean areas. Our analysis also revealed that the Cox and Munk wave-crest standard deviation wind-speed relationship underestimates wind speed at low values due to the influence of gravity waves, which the original model does not fully account for. Furthermore, our results indicate that the Cox and Munk spectral peak period-wind speed formula does not take into consideration the impact of deep water conditions on wave conditions.

The primary challenge in testing large-scale software frameworks is the sheer number of possible test combinations. To address this issue, a research team proposed an algorithm that efficiently selects an optimal set of test scenarios to maximize defect detection capabilities. This algorithm was originally implemented using Python, but its sequential processing limited scalability for larger software frameworks. To overcome this limitation, a research group developed a parallelized algorithm based on parallel unique value decomposition. By leveraging the parallel capabilities, this enhanced algorithm significantly reduced computational time and memory usage, making it more suitable for evaluating large-scale software frameworks.

Social media platforms often reflect the true sentiments and emotions of society, and can significantly influence and be influenced by societal norms. Analyzing the emotions within microblogs has become an essential tool for tracking the true nature of the pandemic and preventing its spread by identifying and countering false rumors. This research presents a comprehensive collection of user emotions within microblogs during the coronavirus outbreak in China, in line with the NRC emotion framework. Initially, basic emotion categories were employed to classify comments within four regions affected by the pandemic: Hubei, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Guangdong. Subsequently, nuanced emotion categories were applied to classify comments in Hubei, revealing the true sentiment of users on social media during the pandemic.

Building a accurate Tai network from ai network data is an exclusive option for
high-voltage and short-distance electrical connections due to its ability to
reduce partial discharges by up to 90% compared to traditional Tai structures.
Recently, a novel partial discharge suppression mechanism called 'Counter Tai' was
introduced, showcasing up to 60% improvement in prevention rates. Nonetheless,
the fabrication of Counter Tai poses significant difficulties, largely stemming from
the impossibility of directly constructing it from ai. We overcame this limitation
by introducing a transformative 'Tai counter' process that derives Counter Tai from
an ai structure, albeit at a reduced level of partial discharge prevention, limited to
approximately 40%-50%. Furthermore, this Tai counter structure maintains symmetry
similar to its Counter Tai counterpart, potentially contributing to its reduced
efficacy in preventing partial discharges. To achieve a Tai counter structure, we

A 2015 generalization of the compressed shift operator by Das, Shum, and Wu is examined, generalizing its properties. The effect of this generalization on the compressive behavior within a specific family of orthogonally multiplicity-free bases is determined. A new class of-compressed Willoughby operators is introduced, and the impact of compression on the Fock space associated with this family is investigated.

A vertical shear instability is proposed to occur at the boundary between gas phases, potentially causing the rapid formation of planetesimals. Researchers believe that objects instigated by this phenomenon would be located in the disk's midplane. In contrast, a dust disk is observed extending above the midplane and stretching towards the disk's surface. An investigation was conducted to determine how including a two-dimensional dust model would affect the one-dimensional shear instability. Results revealed that interaction with the two-dimensional component of gas led to a two-way influence. On one hand, shear forces contributed to cooling the upper regions of the disk midplane and potentially contributed to forming planetesimals. On the other hand, instability led to increased formation of rocks. These results indicated that including a two-dimensional dust model was crucial for comprehending the mechanisms of the one-dimensional shear instability and that it might be a significant factor in explaining the surface structures of gas planets.

This paper investigates the Liouville property in the context of manifolds with a lower bound on Ricci curvature, constant scalar curvature, and a measure that decreases linearly. We establish a specific bound on the dimension for non-existence of positive functions with a bounded Laplacian. The results are applied to obtain uniform Poincaré and Sobolev inequalities within these geometric frameworks.

Recently, Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks have excelled in generating condition-specific data. To enhance their capability of learning conditional data that includes everything from low to high points on a continuum, it is crucial to enable both end conditions to contribute to the generation at any intermediate point. However, achieving this balance proves challenging as the networks may become confused about the significance of each condition during intermediate points. This study proposes a solution to this problem by proposing dynamic entrance modules that are sensitive to each condition and can adapt to each end condition, as well as a global mean pooling module that sums up the global average of each condition to prevent any unnecessary components from being produced at extreme points. Experimental evaluations with multiple datasets, including MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR10, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model in terms of generation quality and diversity, as well as its ability to achieve smooth transitions with continuous conditions through the use of the SWDN dataset.

The complexity of mathematical models used to simulate dynamic systems can hinder our understanding and subsequent management of those systems. Consequently, model simplification is a crucial step in this process. While model simplification techniques are well-established for linear systems, the equivalent procedures for nonlinear systems are significantly more computationally demanding. This paper presents a novel, efficient method for simplifying nonlinear models directly from observed data, leveraging iterative linear regression within a limited time window and utilizing sparse solvers for rapid over-determined equation resolution. Our results show that this method can achieve high levels of model fidelity with reduced complexity, surpassing current standards in computational time.

A new class of objects called self-boosted solitons is identified within relativistic theories of symmetry breaking. These self-boosted solitons are characterized by their finite mass and spin, remaining stable under a range of boost transformations. Under certain conditions, they can also coexist with charge within non-Abelian gauge theories. The existence of these objects is confirmed through rigorous mathematical proof, multiscaling analysis, and numerical simulation. The theoretical framework for their construction is developed in both $SU(2)$ Skyrme and Leutwyler models, demonstrating that they form in anti-critical regimes of parameter values. Additionally, it is shown that charge can be acquired in both models, occurring either in the core or on the surface of these objects. The construction of self-boosted solitons in an $O(3)$ sigma model is also demonstrated. These findings provide a foundation for future exploration into the design of objects with combined charge, spin, and boosted symmetry in more complex theoretical models.

This article presents an improved version of a previously developed secure
machine learning technique called SIMC, which is robust against a malicious client.
The initial SIMC system utilized a secure two-party computation method based on a
homomorphic encryption scheme called Paillier to protect the inference step of a
support vector machine. This simulation proved that SIMC effectively prevents
data and model information leakage to a malicious client, while incurring
significant communication and computation costs. To address the high inefficiency
of the previous system, the authors have now created SIMC 2.0, a novel approach
that utilizes a different homomorphic encryption technique called RLWE and a
multi-point evaluation method. Since BGV/RNS is not semantically secure, the authors
have proved that the proposed method achieves a secure computation outcome
equivalent to that of SIMC 2.0 through a transformation theorem. Furthermore,
multiple performance tests have demonstrated that in comparison to SIMC, SIMC 2.0
achieves up to an order of magnitude improvement in both computation and
communication efficiency.

We utilized the 1-min sensitivity of the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Sensitive radio telescope to study the M101 galaxy group's 14 cm hydrogen lines, which we observed in 11 units of frequency from 11 spectral lines. Our high-resolution spectral lines allowed us to calculate the relative velocities of each galaxy with a maximum error margin of 20 km/s. Our observations revealed that there are at least 11 hidden galaxies in this group that have been previously undetected, and we also discovered a spiral arm or tail made of hydrogen gas as extended as 70 thousand light-years from galaxy NGC 5194. We found that this tail may have been formed by a tidal interaction or a tidal wave between the two galaxies, and we also noticed that there are at least 11 hidden galaxies in this group that have been previously undetected, and we also discovered a spiral arm or tail made of hydrogen gas as extended as 70 thousand light-years from galaxy NGC 5194. We found that this tail may have been formed by a tidal interaction or a tidal wave between the two galaxies.

To tackle challenges in answering questions that require thinking outside the box in areas unrelated to their main topic, current Response Generation models tend to prioritize quantity over quality in their possible responses, resulting in satisfactory answers among many incorrect ones. To address this issue, we introduce a novel approach called Semantic-connected Insight (ScIns), which is designed to help models narrow down choices while focusing on relevant information. We incorporate this design into an existing framework to answer questions that require reasoning about general knowledge and common sense, testing the efficacy of our approach on three different evaluation metrics. Our experiments demonstrate that adding ScIns not only improves model performance but also reduces the number of inaccurate responses when outside experts rate them, particularly for questions that are more complex and difficult to answer, according to Lewis et al., 2019, and Sun et al., 2019. To further validate our approach, we provide a detailed analysis of the top three responses that are considered correct, along with corresponding examples, in our study,认真落实每个步骤, 引入外部专家评价, 对生成答案进行主观评估, 统计并可视化结果, 以此证明 ScIns 的有效性与可靠性, 尤其是对于需要广泛知识的推理, 我们的方法表现优异, 显著减少了一倍以上的不正确回答, 当外部专家对排名靠前的回答进行评价时, 至少有一个回答被判定为正确, 统计结果表明, 引入 ScIns 后, 模型的回答被外部专家判定为正确的

The complex chemical reactions occurring in the cometary coma can create a wide range of positively charged molecular compounds that include oxygen bonded to other elements or in the form of carbonyl groups. The impact of sunlight on these compounds as well as their subsequent interaction with neutral molecules or other charged particles can generate ultraviolet and visible light through the process of photon emission. The study of these composite spectra, specifically in the UV to visible range, can provide valuable information about the composition of the coma. The complexity of this chemical composition can be better understood through this analysis. Our report discusses various oxygen-bearing molecular cations such as H_2O^+, CO_2^+, and their potential role in contributing to the observed spectral features. The provided data on their emission properties, presented as tables or graphs, can aid researchers in distinguishing between the emissions from these molecular cations and their relative significance in contributing to the cometary spectra. This information is expected to contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of the chemistry occurring in cometary comae when observed through spectroscopic analysis.

This research investigates the representation of a number $n$ as a sum of squares of four distinct global algebraic quantities - S-integers, number fields, function fields, and $v$-adic fields - with the constraint that $n$ must be less than or equal to the product of their dimensions. For S-integers, we establish that almost all numbers can be represented under this constraint, confirming a conjecture by V. K. Kumar. For number fields, we prove that very few numbers cannot be represented, specifically at most four. In the case of biquadratic number fields, the count of exceptions cannot exceed the count of quadratic fields with infinite real places. For function fields over a finite field with $q$ elements, the number of representations cannot exceed $\frac{6(q-1)}{q+1}$. Finally, for local fields of characteristic zero, the maximum number of representations cannot be exceeded by three.

The vast amounts of optical/infrared spectroscopic data being produced by
current and upcoming telescopes are making it increasingly difficult to
correlate different datasets to construct comprehensive object catalogs. This
challenge is exacerbated by the upcoming high-throughput facilities of major
survey telescopes such as DESI, HSC, and DESIRE. To overcome these
cross-correlation difficulties, a novel approach is proposed that combines
simple spectral analyzers with traditional methods to achieve accurate and
efficient spectro-to-photonic cross-correlations, a concept illustrated
through a case study comparing the SDSS and the Pan-STARRS1 surveys. This
approach is further explored through recommendations for future facilities
like the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, showcasing the potential of
astrophotonic science to effectively cross-correlate spectra and photometrics
to produce optimized master catalogs enriched with both photometric and
spectral properties for a wide range of scientific studies.

High-performance models that rely on representing relationships have significantly contributed to various fields of clinical research. Using pre-trained models based on relationships has traditionally been shown to be more effective than other techniques in certain tasks, such as assessing how medications interact. This paper provides a cohesive overview of the integration of learning relationships in clinical data models and models that utilize relationships. The focus is on models that learn relationships between medications through embeddings and examines the advancements in models that utilize relationships for evaluating the interaction between medications. The model cohorts and publicly available datasets for evaluating the interaction between medications are also discussed for the benefit of future research in this field.
We derive a generalized It\^o-Wentzell formula for the change of variable in the context of uneven paths within the Wasserer space, building upon previous work by Gangbo, Nguyen, and Panaretos.

A significant challenge in Federated Learning (FedLearn) is that the local data is often non-I.I.D., which hampers the model's ability to learn effectively. To address this issue, we propose an innovative approach called Random Stroll Learning (RbSl), a new framework that goes beyond standard FedLearn by allowing clients to share model updates with neighboring clients in addition to the server. RbSl is capable of learning from a diverse data distribution where the client data distribution changes over time. We provide a theoretical analysis of RbSl and establish a mathematical relationship between the client data distribution and the improved FedLearn model. The dynamic and flexible nature of the communication pattern in RbSl makes it particularly well-suited for resolving the data scarcity and data distribution issues in FedLearn. The experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of RbSl, which significantly outperforms existing FedLearn baselines in various scenarios.

We have developed a numerical method to simulate three-dimensional chaotic flow patterns caused by random oscillations at two parallel planes, which is known to be a type of inertial wave chaos. This methodology is used to simulate 3D flows with Lagrangian tracers, producing a clear and verified proof of the $E\propto f^{5/3}$ energy spectrum in the inertial spectrum range, an hallmark of these types of chaotic flows. Our findings are obtained from direct numerical simulations rather than spectral analysis, a first in the study of inertial wave chaos.

The effects of mandatory therapy for imprisoned individuals on their psychological well-being and desistance from criminal activities are explored in this study. A distinctive dataset from the US allows us to estimate the causal impact of mandatory court-ordered treatment on incarceration duration, release outcomes, reoffending rates, and various psychological indicators. Our findings suggest that mandatory treatment has a positive, significant causal effect on several indicators of psychological well-being and is associated with increased time spent in prison and higher likelihood of successful releases. Furthermore, we discover that mandatory treatment has varying impacts on release type and reoffending rates across different subgroups of prisoners, with notable increases in psychological well-being among youth offenders leading to higher rates of successful releases.

A widely-used regularization method in computer vision tasks is the L1 norm, which forms the basis of several cutting-edge semi-supervised healthcare image segmentation techniques. These techniques combine supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, utilizing mask consistency and feature consistency as their primary mechanisms. Implementing these techniques in a framework based on the PatchTask network has yielded impressive results in segmenting complex healthcare images. Nevertheless, achieving optimal performance typically demands significant computational resources and extensive hyperparameter tuning. We propose a novel approach, the normalized consistency regularization (NCR) model, which extends the Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) model. The NCR model normalizes the combined predictions of the teacher and student networks, allowing for the application of the L1 norm. We demonstrate the superiority of the NCR model over the NMSE model on three diverse and clinically demanding healthcare image datasets.

The ATLAS Jet Calorimeter Trigger (L1TAoR) requires a significant amount of through-board and buffer bandwidth at an impressive rate of 288 GB/s, necessitating high-performance electronics. A new board based on the Xilinx UltraScale+ architecture offers 10x this bandwidth while maintaining cost-effectiveness. This board features six 10Gbps Optical Transceiver Cards (OCS) for through-board bandwidth and 48 Front-End Processor Boards (FEPs) connected via Cable dA, each with 512 (16x32) Gbps of bandwidth. The board runs the complete FEP software from the ATLAS, achieving a system throughput of 32 GB/s in end-to-end tests. As such, it is well-suited for upgrading the ATLAS detector for Phase-2 of the LHC.

This paper introduces a novel approach to creating realistic animations for complex, multi-part characters known as articulated figures. We combine neural network fields with rigid animations to develop a convertible and realistic depiction. Our method allows for efficient transformations between different representations, providing a compact model capable of animating multiple distinct characters simultaneously. By using a shared representation, we facilitate easy conversions and realistic simulations. Experimental results show superior performance compared to existing approaches, demonstrating our method's effectiveness through various virtual avatar animations.

The high sensitivity to initial conditions that characterizes chaotic systems poses a significant challenge in predicting their behavior. Therefore, effectively assessing chaos within domains such as turbulence is of paramount importance but remains elusive due to its complex nature. In this study, we present a novel, high-throughput approach for evaluating local chaos by utilizing graph neural networks to analyze the dynamics of a single atom within a two-body chaotic system, such as that of Rydberg atoms. This method provides a valuable tool for studying the intricate dynamics of chaotic systems and their implications for understanding turbulence and other complex phenomena.

Estimating the average of a parameter from multiple sources or varieties is an ananlyssis used in various fields including biology, chemistry, geology, and social sciences. We investigate the likelihood ratio and generalized likelihood ratio tests for accurately estimating the average of a parameter from multiple sources in a sampling context. The ratio of these test statistics follows a chi-squared distribution at a null hypothesis, and we establish this relationship through theoretical derivation and support it with empirical evidence from simulations and real-world data.

Educators and researchers are constantly seeking improved teaching and learning methods, with one area of focus being the application of Data Science and Machine Learning in Education. Among these applications is Knowledge Tracing, a student modeling task that predicts a learner's grasp of a specific subject at a given time. This prediction is essential for the development of adaptive learning systems. Traditional Knowledge Tracing methods are generally black-box systems that lack transparency. To address this, three novel explainable Knowledge Tracing models based on Interpretable Linear Neural Networks were presented. These models not only predicted student performance accurately, but also provided an interpretation of their findings. Three evaluation metrics were used to assess the effectiveness of these models, with results indicating that they performed comparably to leading Knowledge Tracing systems. Furthermore, a Python framework called pypy was created to facilitate the testing and comparison of Knowledge Tracing systems.

This paper proves that for a second-order elliptic operator L on a non-compact space X, its harmonic functions naturally belong to all Lebesgue spaces $L^p$ at once. This key property is established by demonstrating the equivalence of the $L^p$-solvability of L with the existence of a harmonic capacity that generates all Lebesgue spaces. Additionally, for a class of non-singular sigma-finite measure spaces, we prove that for 1<p<infty, the following statements are equivalent: the existence of a harmonic capacity equivalent to the norm of functions in the Dirichlet space, and the uniform isomorphic embedding of the harmonic functions into all Lebesgue spaces. Consequently, for 1<p<infty, L is found to have a restricted range.

This format, called Alethe, is an ANI representation that utilizes Unicode characters and has been adopted by various proof formats including Isar, Coq, and Mette. The althe proof format is designed to be both human-readable and machine-processable, with machine-checking performed by the Alethe theorem prover. The format's key feature is its reliance on a set of rewrite rules, such as associativity, commutativity, and uniqueness of names, to reconcile different notations and terms, with the choice of proving terms left to the user. The format is also accompanied by a suite of sanitization tools that include a set of backends for converting proofs from various formats to Alethe.

In the context of federated learning, we have identified a consistent pattern of behavior that mirrors the characteristics of unconstrained gradient descent methods. This discovery comes from our analysis of how buffers are used to store updates on client devices before they are aggregated with the global model. We have further demonstrated that, in highly dynamic client environments, buffered aggregation results in similar performance and efficiency outcomes to unconstrained methods, with nearly the same reduction in model training iterations and up to 40% less overhead for data transfer. The findings of our research led us to propose a buffer parameter that optimizes performance in federated methods by testing multiple configurations and selecting the most effective. The superiorperformed by our method surpasses the typical performance of buffered approaches by an increment of 2 iterations and 3% of overhead. The proposed method exhibits robustness across different optimization techniques, model architectures, optimization techniques, model architectures, hyperparameter configurations, we evaluated the efficacy of our method across multiple model architectures, hyperparameter configurations, and federated learning setups.

Lately, automatic speech recognition systems have achieved remarkable success in processing clear speech, yet fewer focus on understanding how clear systems can be adapted to recognize less comprehensible data. This study investigates the concept of transfer learning from clear to ambiguous data across different languages, utilizing transfer transfer learning. We have conducted experiments transferring models from clear-to-noisy data and from one language to another, in this case English-to-German, in order to examine how these transfers interact. Our findings from these experiments led to a novel approach of reverse transfer, essentially going from ambiguous-to-clear-data-and-one-language. Our reverse transfer model showed significant improvements in accuracy compared to standard training on ambiguous data, and also performed well when compared to models using just transfer learning.

Our research aims at embedding nodes in Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) using their spatial coordinates, a task made relevant by the increasing prevalence of project management tools that utilize Gantt charts. Evaluating the effectiveness of such embeddings is a novel challenge, as there is an established standard for similarity-measuring techniques but not for dash- and tree-orientation methods. To address this lack, our work introduces a pioneering dataset and evaluation framework for assessing DAG-orientation performance. We created the Twitch Players dataset, comprising over 10^5 nodes, representing the structure of a league table for the 2016-2017 European Championship season. Evaluating our approach, our results indicate that methods like HillClimbing achieved an effective dash-orientation, resulting in a 22% reduction in horizontal depth compared to alternative embeddings.

Our study focuses on the distinction between two theories regarding the nature of $f_X(1500)$, a resonance that has various claimed relationships with the $\rho^0(1450)$ and $f_2(1420)$, but lacks a clear explanation. By using an amplitude analysis consistent with experimental evidence from the Belle collaboration, specifically from studies on $B\to \pi\pi\pi\pi$ decays, we derive a reliable fit to this resonance. Through examination of $B^0\to K^+K^-\pi^+\pi^-$ decays with the assistance of artificial intelligence techniques, we locate the $\rho^0(1450)$ within the $K^+K^-$ spectrum of $\rho^-\to \pi^+\rho^0$ transitions. This new resonance is found to have unique properties, differing from previously understood $f_2(1420)$ and $\rho^0(1450)$ resonances. Additionally, we present arguments that $f_X(1420)$ and $\rho^0(1450)$ are actually two separate resonances.

The addition of two modern cosmological phenomena, the dark energy component and the dark matter component, to the standard model of particle physics necessitates new theoretical frameworks. This paper proposes a novel perspective, suggesting that dark energy and dark matter may both be attributed to an enigmatic third category - a fifth dimension known as the "Marshland." Focusing on a specific theory involving primordial black holes as the composition of dark matter, this study calculates the properties of these primordial black holes that would result in the correct dark matter density. It further demonstrates that, depending on the model parameters, such as those involving the production rate of primordial black holes and the subsequent accretion of radiation by them, the "dark photon lifetime" - defined as the point in time when the primordial black holes constitute only a fraction of the dark matter density - occurred within the period leading up to the nucleosynthesis period.

Force control systems with series elastic actuators are highly beneficial for collaborative robots due to their safety and interactive capabilities, and their performance is significantly influenced by the choice of transmission force estimator. This study aims to enhance the accuracy of force regulation through a novel strong transmission force estimator that effectively counters the elastic oscillations caused by the series spring. The proposed estimator uses an integrated low-pass filter to more precisely estimate the transmission force, with its performance validated using experimental testing across various frequency ranges. Results show that the proposed estimator outperforms traditional methods, and this study also provides insights into selecting an optimal low-pass filter time constant for optimal control performance, and these findings are supported by systematic experimental tests performed on a dual-spring actuated testbed.

Liquid crystals are used extensively as teaching tools and widely in applications, with micro-rheology being one such example. The commonly used particles for this purpose are nearly spherical, yet they can develop defects that impede their performance. Our study utilizes a computational model of colloidal eukaryotic cytoskeletal networks, which assembles into structures similar to 'bars', discovering that defects within these 'bars' cause them to shatter. The phenomenon of fracture is found to be triggered by the bending of these structures, with internal stresses accumulating until they result in failure, which aligns with engineering principles of bending moments. The theoretical implications of this discovery are vast, with potential applications in understanding the causes of cellular damage from external forces, as many cells possess curved structures that may shatter due to this very mechanism.

We investigated a lattice SU(Nc) gauge theory in 3D that includes interactions for scalars spanning multiple representations of Su(Nc). These interactions influence the lattice phase diagram by modifying the symmetry-breaking phase transitions of the gauge or the Higgs phase transitions directly or indirectly. Introducing an electric field on the boundary changes the transition to a phase where the color electric field is confined. For sufficiently large fundamental representation charge, this transition becomes first-order. Additionally, introducing an adjoint representation electric field changes the confinement transition. For sufficiently large fundamental representation charge, this phase transition shifts from second to first-order. Consequently, this indicates that the 2d confinement phase boundary can be altered from second to first-order without entering a distinct phase, merely by altering the strength of the scalar-higgs interaction. We observed similar phenomena in lattice SU(3) gauge theory.

Achieving fully autonomous navigation for underwater robots without human intervention or pre-defined maps proves to be a challenging task. A significant breakthrough occurred in 2007 with the launch of HAILIEU 2.0, an underwater robot that demonstrated fully autonomous navigation from start to finish. This was made possible due to its advanced navigation system, TV-L-GPSM, an innovative approach to navigating the robot through sparsely available visual landmarks that change over time. This achievement has been rare in the field of underwater robotics. As underwater exploration continues, developing fully autonomous navigation systems for robots becomes increasingly crucial. Consequently, researchers are investing significant effort in this area of development. In this paper, we delve into the autonomous navigation approach of the HAILIEU 2.0 robot, detailing its successful implementation of fully autonomous navigation. We also outline the challenges associated with developing navigation systems for underwater robots. Furthermore, we introduce our Gaussian Process-based landmark detection model and our autonomous navigation framework. Lastly, we provide an overview of the challenges that lie ahead in the path of fully autonomous underwater robot navigation.

This paper identifies optimal sorting networks for any size, those with uniformly deep structures, and focuses particularly on networks with minimal, 2k-stage depths for inputs n = 3 × 2^(k-1). We discover the first optimal uniform-depth networks for k values ranging from 3.5 to 12, and propose a general method to find such networks for any k, overcoming previous limitations imposed by the $\Theta(n \log n)$ bound. Additionally, we investigate non-uniform depth networks and establish record-low 2k-stage depth records for n = 28, 30, 32, 36, 42, 48, 54, and 64 (with k = 9), as well as 2k+1-stage depth records for n = 29, 33, 35, 43, 47, 54, 54, 55, 56, 57, 63, 65 (with k = 9).

In General Relativity, non-uniform fluids composed of two components under self-gravity and modeled by the Einstein field equations have been analyzed. Specifically, we investigate an anisotropic fluid, whose pressure varies due to a power-law relationship with density, that contains an additional component expanding at a constant rate. This model, which can describe celestial bodies like planets with convection layers or stars with cores and envelopes, is shown to fulfill all necessary conditions for physical viability. Furthermore, the model can reproduce known monofluid solutions when one of the two components is made negligible.

The formation mechanisms of spiral structures in galaxy disks remain a mystery to astronomers, thus we developed a computer simulation of a multi-component galaxy similar to the Milky Way to investigate their origin.  Utilizing an $N$-body simulation, we replicated a two-quadruplet galaxy similar to the Milky Way, consisting of a bulge, disk, dark halo, and bar, over 8 billion years.  We observed that a fraction of the bulge, dark halo, and bar populations developed into spiral patterns after being perturbed by an off-center subhalo with about $10^{11} M_{\odot}$ mass that passed close to the galaxy's center, 2 billion years into the simulation.  We discovered that the subhalo contributed very little to the outer gas disk's spiral formation.  We believe that the central bar, due to its resonance, played a significant role in creating the spiral pattern near the galaxy's center, contributing to the box/pearl appearance of inner spirals, and that the outer spiral's formation was likely caused by the outer ring, whose formation was triggered by a resonance associated with the galaxy's bar and subhalo.

The impact of magnetic fields on galaxy collisions is still not well understood. To investigate this, we ran advanced computer simulations of two colliding galaxies with and without magnetic fields. The simulations included intricate physical processes such as gravity, collisions between particles, and the conversion of matter into energy. We observed that magnetic fields experienced by a galaxy through its collision are typically stretched, leading to increased intensity in some areas. The orientation of these magnetic fields is generally aligned with the galaxy's collidal field, showing a perpendicular relationship with the boundary between the two colliding galaxies in about half of the simulation time. The intensity of these magnetic fields varies over time at a scale of approximately 10^3 parsecs, which has a direct impact on a phenomenon called magnetic diffusion. This influence is comparable to the one exerted by turbulent flows, and as a result, the stars and gas in these galaxies tend to follow similar distribution patterns.

The recent pandemic of COVID-19 has significantly impacted nearly 190 countries, with over 14 million confirmed cases claiming more than one lakh lives globally. Effective measures such as social distancing, hand hygiene, and wearing masks have proven crucial for containing its spread, yet the virus continues to pose a substantial threat due to varying intensities within infected individuals, necessitating a tailored approach to manage different severity levels. In this context, a machine learning capability that accurately identifies the intensity of infections based on CT scans would greatly aid in managing the pandemic by enabling rapid diagnosis and treatment planning. Addressing the limitations of existing classification approaches that struggle with insufficient and unbalanced training data, a novel technique named IAMNet was introduced to tackle the challenge of five-way partial classification using only a small number of training images, integrating innovative techniques like contrastive loss and data augmentation through external sources to enhance performance and efficiency. Experimental outcomes showcase IAMNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods on two prominent datasets representing different COVID cases.

Most current sequence-to-sequence based machine translation systems produce output of high quality when ample data is available, but they struggle with accuracy in fewer data scenarios or when dealing with unbalanced pairs of source and target languages. Research has been conducted to develop sentence-level machine translation models capable of correcting errors in written English by using paired sentences, where one is error-free and the other contains multiple types of mistakes. However, such models are reliant on multi-fold datasets and their performance significantly declines in cases where only single-type data is used for training. The issue of using paired sentences, where one is error-free and the other contains multiple types of mistakes, to train models for error correction remains largely unexplored. To tackle models that are exposed to diverse types of errors in written English, this study proposes a method of domain transfer in which models are trained on one type of mistake and then applied to correct another type of error. The model's weights are fine-tuned with an auxiliary loss function that encourages distributional similarity between errors and targets. The proposed approach is evaluated through few-shot experiments conducted on two pairs of error types from the British National Corpus and the XGLUE benchmark. The results show that our proposed method yields substantial improvements over baseline models in terms of model efficacy.

When rounding rates, percentages, or averages to a certain decimal place or whole number, discrepancies arise between the calculated average of rounded numbers and the rounded sum of original numbers. This phenomenon is explored this study by providing an algebraic framework and stochastic model to quantify and anticipate variations in a calculated total from presenting data as an average, specifically when relying on rounded integers. Key factors influencing these deviations in accounting for attendance at meetings based on registration rates from survey questions are identified, and potential applications involving estimation of meeting attendance and dataset totals are highlighted.

Researchers investigated the crystal structure, as well as the electronic and magnetic properties of single-crystalline GdInO$_3$, utilizing X-ray diffraction, X-photoelectron spectroscopy, and measurements of its DC electrical conductivity, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat. Despite initial expectations based on Gd-based oxide behavior, GdInO$_3$ was found to be an indirect band gap semiconductor in contrast to direct band gap observations for related compounds. Furthermore, GdInO$_3$ was classified as a centered honeycomb magnet with two distinct subsets of 4f moments that interact through both direct and mediate exchanges, resulting in two inequivalent susceptibility peaks. This behavior was consistent with its two-dimensional centered honeycomb lattice structure.

We investigate the connection between cooperative and non-cooperative games in the context of providing non-transferable, discrete resources to self-interested agents. A resource allocation among agents in a cooperative setting is considered, and we examine whether there always exists an equilibrium in a subsequent game where each agent either accepts or rejects their allocated resource. Our primary objective is to achieve an allocation with at least one agent receiving their desired resource.

Surprisingly, we discovered that for standard preference relations, the answer is indeed always affirmative for specific resources, such as new employees being assigned to teams or group projects being assigned to teams. In these cases, we established efficient algorithms to determine whether there always exists an equilibrium containing a specific preference-sharing bundle. Moreover, we developed parametrized approaches to this problem.

Nevertheless, the answer becomes negative when agents' preferences involve more complex comparison outcomes, such as preferring a resource over rejection, being indifferent, or dispreference. Here, we developed efficient algorithms to solve this problem for specific resources, particularly for two units of an identical item. Additionally, we explored connections to equity, discovering that when agents' preferences strictly differentiate between resources and rejection, the answer is always affirmative for at least a 1/2 fraction of agents that can be satisfied within a pure Nash equilibrium allocation. For standard preference relations, we discovered that the Nash equilibrium value can be improved to at least a 1/2 fraction of agents considering a specific preference-sharing bundle, and this equity parameter can be further

The prevalent methods for removing unwanted labels from videos frequently depend heavily on supervised domain translation, often resulting in distorted output videos due to one-to-many real world mappings. In this study, we investigate non-deterministic transformations in the absence of human label information. Our approach utilizes generative adversarial networks to map source images to a collection of domain-specific target images. We incorporate unsupervised classification and a novel competitive loss function to ensure that each potential target image remains easily identifiable. The proposed method is tested for its ability to convert videos of one-to-many objects such as face expressions, hand gestures, and scene lighting conditions. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance when compared to previous approaches in terms of low reconstruction errors and high classification accuracy, all without the need for target image labels.

We have discovered an ultra-stable disk (USD) in galaxy UGC 8839, a rare and isolated case. This USD, located near the inner edge of the optical disk, is stable over time and doesn't significantly emit light. It's an intriguing region to study as it's isolated from the central bulge disk and the outer parts of the galaxy. In contrast, other spiral galaxies usually have more extensive USDs with larger semi-major axes. Observations of six additional galaxies, including three early-type spirals, show that ultra-stable disks are a common and dominant component of the disk population, not anomalies.

The proposed paleo-detectors, utilizing ancient limestone as a detection medium, have successfully identified multiple dark matter candidates and tightly constrained other types of particles that interact weakly with matter. This review discusses the scientific knowledge gained from PALAEo-Detectors (PALEOs) and the potential for future paleo-detectors to explore darker sectors of matter-labeled PALEOs 2.0. Notably, 2.0 detectors could also take on the role of safeguarding other types of research, such as neutrino studies and multi-messenger astronomy, against interference from terrestrial sources. The characteristics required for ideal detector materials in the context of paleo-detectors are outlined, and a proposal for experimental validation with simulated events on laboratory materials is presented.

This paper introduces a novel differential privacy technique, DP-Sync, for protecting a common challenge in securely outsourced databases. In these systems, clients outsource their data to untrusted servers and employ privacy techniques like Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to prevent data leakage. It's well-documented that an observer can infer information about the data by analyzing patterns in update queries, even when the content of the updates remains encrypted. To address this issue, existing research has focused on adding privacy to queries or bulk data export, but not on obscuring the update pattern itself. In contrast, our proposed DP-Sync framework leverages differential privacy to hide trends in update queries. By randomly exporting subsets of data and performing query updates in smaller batches, DP-Sync ensures that no single entity has access to more than a certain amount of information about the data, measured by the $\epsilon$ parameter of differential privacy. We evaluated the practicality of DP-Sync by integrating it with the PUFFIN database system and observing that its overhead remains within a reasonable range, typically under 10x for common $\epsilon$ values.

Decision tree-based machine learning methods are known for their straightforward design, yet they suffer from inherent instability and overfitting issues. One solution to mitigate these drawbacks involves ensemble techniques that combine multiple decision trees through techniques like bagging and boosting. Specifically, Random Forest has emerged as a highly effective methodology that boasts superior performance, interpretability and robustness against adversarial manipulation. Through rigorous experimentation involving diverse machine learning algorithms across five datasets, this study confirms that Random Forest delivers optimal performance that surpasses alternatives like support vector machines, logistic regression, and mutual information techniques. Furthermore, our research demonstrates that incorporating Mutually Unbiased Basis (MUC) to expand the initial tree structure of a Random Forest yields enhanced feature significance assessment, protects against biased information injection, and facilitates a more reliable evaluation of feature importance.

Minimally invasive surgery has been made easier with the development of advanced surgical tools, and automatic surgical tool segmentation has been further facilitated by progress in computer vision and deep learning. This paper focuses on the challenge of instant surgical tool segmentation in minimally invasive surgery, where models must predict tool positions from past video frames. To tackle this challenge, we explore several deep learning approaches, including fully convolutional networks and dilated convolutional networks. Our results show that a simple fully convolutional network with 2048 filters and 5 dilated dilation rates slightly outperforms the baseline, achieving an intersection over union of 0.8597. This model is robust and delivers consistent performance across 100 video samples.

Individual re-identification refers to the task of locating a specific person among numerous other individuals, and it is essential in various applications, particularly in ensuring the safety of vital areas. Traditionally, this task has been accomplished using closed-world protocols that rely on training data matching the query. However, comparing this to multi-label re-identification where labels are assigned to multiple individuals, or cross-world re-identification, task. In this paper, we introduce a dataset called MERBARD, which is an extensive unsupervised dataset collected in the medical domain to evaluate the feasibility of individual re-identification in these settings. MERBARD consists of 277 subjects and includes images from different cameras, styles, datasets, and locations. A significant finding of our research is that even under unsupervised conditions, training models with contrastive learning enables them to effectively perform the re-identification task. A significant outcome of our research is the creation of the MERBARD benchmark, which evaluates the performance of various methods and models for re-identification in this dataset.

This paper presents a novel Bayesian framework called achThreshold measurement, which is derived from the Generalized Auto-Conditional Heteroskedasticity model. The framework incorporates an asymmetric dependence structure to track real-time financial data, with a specific emphasis on predicting extreme market movements in the bottom quartile.采用数据仿真和真实市场数据检验, 结果 显示 该框架 有效 预测 了标普 500 指数 和 中 国 A 股 市场 的 极端 波动, 表现 不 差 于 现 有 最 先进 的 GARCH 框架. 相 较 于 传统 的 TGARCH 模型, 我 们 的 框架 用 更 少 的 参 数 达 到 更 为 准 确 的 风 险 预 测, 且 中 国 A 股 市场 的 实 例 验 证 揭 示 该 框 架 可 能 帮 助 外 资 投 资 者 预 测 中 国 政 策 所 引 起 的 突 然 市 场 下 跌.

Using data from pulsar timing arrays, we've developed a method to calculate the gravitational wave recoil phenomenon. A specific combination of gravitational wave modes represents the mass change due to the ejection of mass during a binary merger. By analyzing existing methods and proposing a new approach, we found that using the change in mass dipole is more feasible for detection with current and future pulsar data. The precision of this estimation relies heavily on future improvements in parameter estimation using various datasets. A high-fidelity numerical simulation has been used to validate this approach.

A theoretical investigation involving two-current correlations in a real-time, real-frequency analysis of interacting fermions within a Dirac Hamiltonian is presented. Specifically, the response of the system to external electromagnetic perturbations that affect the pion form factor is examined at various momentum values and is validated through lattice discretization. The findings reveal the preservation of gauge invariance in the lattice results. A significant indication of quark confinement is identified as an exponential decay in the form factor beyond 1 GeV/c, with the decay intensity related to the string tension. A semi-classical analysis is also performed to derive the kinematical variations in the form factor and validate these findings with lattice simulations.

Accretion processes in planetary-forming disks are thought to drive the growth of stars, and thus far believed to be a steady process. Yet, recent evidence indicates that this process may be highly variable. This research aims to shed light on the nature of this fluctuation by examining a case that exhibits particularly dramatic changes – the L T Tauri star XX Cha. Observations conducted with the ESPRESSO spectrograph at the Very Large Telescope (VLT) indicate that XX Cha's line-driven H$\alpha$ flux displays extreme variability on timescales of days to weeks. Furthermore, its variability does not correlate with the stability typically observed in its near-infrared flux. These findings suggest that accretion rates in XX Cha are extremely unpredictable. Estimations of the accretion rates from its spectral lines and optical variability in the near-infrared in turn suggest a wide range of outcomes – in turn indicating that in systems like this, the accretion rates can vary by as much as four orders of magnitude.

This paper delves into a poetically nicknamed economic concept, 'Inequity of Chance,' which examines the effects of chance on societal income inequality. By utilizing a stochastic general equilibrium model, we investigate how random shock-based inequality impacts the real economy, particularly in the context of unanticipated tax changes. Our analysis reveals that inequity of chance can drive significant income inequality, potentially overshadowing inequalities stemming from skill disparities. Furthermore, we examine the concept of progressive taxation as means of mitigating the inequalities exacerbated by chance within the general equilibrium framework.

Consider a pair of arbitrary flags within a complex semisimple Lie group, and let their intersection form a subvariety. Our primary discovery provides a quantum Birkhoff isomorphism for this space at a generic intersection. This result, achieved through the utilization of degenerate affine Weyl group actions that preserve quantum cohomology, takes the form of an LHS-congruence featuring Chern classes. By establishing a foundation using the type A case, our approach extends to all other types, and contributes a detailed analysis of the degenerate affine action's within-group elements' quantum coroot sum decomposition.

The intricate interplay of vast, multifaceted data sets and complex, decentralized machine learning (ML) architectures in the era of Industry 4.0 presents significant challenges for system administrators and engineers. A primary concern is pinpointing which aspects of data or components of the ML workflow are negatively impacting performance. To address this challenge, we propose using End-2-End ML workflows for automated production troubleshooting and introduce a novel approach for identifying significant data elements or stages by leveraging the Shapley value concept from the game theory. Lbuilding upon this theoretical framework, we present a practical, efficient algorithm that incorporates the SHARP method to efficiently estimate Shapley values, and we empirically validate our approach on real-world scenarios involving significant image classification datasets and industrial sensor-based fault detection workflows.

We explored the connection between X-ray emissions and radio communications within four distinct clusters of stars, specifically choosing the MAVERIC clusters (NGC 288, NGC 5139, NGC 5287, and NGC 6752), comprising low-energy X-ray sources and the diverse spectral types of radio sources, in a significant statistical finding. Using high-resolution X-ray and radio observations, we analyzed these BEERS clusters (BEnign Ultra-dense RElative to sPhellies) at various distances and ages, representing an extensive range of conditions in the galaxy. These four clusters differ notably in density and have been impacted by the tidal forces of the galaxy in diverse ways. We examined the relationship between X-ray and radio emissions across these clusters, focusing on how they vary with cluster conditions and the characteristics of individual radio sources, specifically their spectral type and dynamic history with the cluster. Each of these BEERS clusters displays a distinct break in the radio spectrum, which serves as an indicator of a critical turnover frequency. However, each cluster exhibits the break at a different wavelength, corresponding to different physical processes governing the relationship between X-ray and radio communications. Additionally, spectral type and dynamic history significantly influence both the radio spectrum and the presence of individual radio sources beyond their cluster's typical morphology. Specific high-energy sources, likely originating from collisions between compact stars, were identified in the core regions of two of the BEERS clusters, providing valuable insights for

Recommended systems based on dual graphs fall short in capturing the complex associations between entities and attribute pairs within multi-dimensional data, particularly when dealing with partial missing information. To address this limitation, we propose GHIpr, a novel hypergraph completion framework that leverages diverse connections between entities and entities to recover a comprehensive set of relationships from the incomplete data. By integrating GHIpr into the missing components, we can unify diverse sources of information within the hypergraph, which we optimize through a set of innovative transformation techniques and a carefully constructed objective function that emphasizes local consistency, hyperedge independence, and graph connectivity. The results demonstrate that GHIpr consistently outperforms existing methods on various datasets, achieving superior performance across seven different hypergraph completion scenarios and delivering state-of-the-art outcomes on six of them.

We employ an entropy-based method to analyze the statistical behavior of a microcavity laser system. By comparing electron density profiles of directionally discharged devices at different bias levels, we identify a critical point where the system transitions from a random to an ordered state. At this pivot point, we observe the emergence of longitudinal discharges, and simultaneously, entropy increases due to the creation of energy barriers. Furthermore, by examining the electron energy distribution, we determine the temperature of the system before and after this critical point, and we propose using entropy as a quantitative metric for phase transitions.

The precise measurement of light emitted by heated atomic groups is achieved using homodyne detection, where the photon correlation data obtained reflects both atomic interactions and quantum noise. The results of this hypothesis test, applied to a Casimir-Polder atomic gas, reveal a decrease in photon correlations as atomic interactions are decreased through increased temperature. The measure of this correlation directly reflects the equation of state for these atomic groups.

Most existing datasets for training reinforcement learning agents in multi-agent environments only provide positive outcome scenarios, overlooking the vast number of potential scenarios that could lead to -1 as a outcome. This limitation necessitates the development of sophisticated reward shaping techniques to guide the agents toward optimal outcomes, a process that often proves challenging and requires substantial initial investment. In contrast, our approach focuses on replicating successful strategies from well-trained teachers in multi-agent settings. By leveraging the concept of relative state values, we design an elegant solution that enables agents to distinguish between favorable and unfavorable outcomes. Furthermore, our technique transcends the restriction of multi-agent environments. It allows for the learning of distinction between good and bad outcomes from a diverse range of datasets, even when these datasets are precompiled. We assess the efficacy of our technique on several datasets, showcasing significant performance enhancements over state-of-the-art methods in offline learning scenarios.

We developed a novel approach for aligning megavoltage images, utilizing deep learning techniques to automatically match 2D images to a 3D treatment plan from earlier simulations. This automatic alignment ensures the treatment target is consistently centered in the 2D images, a critical step in image-guided radiotherapy. Our method involves training a specialized neural network configuration on 2D megavoltage images, which was testet on five different datasets representing various types of tumors. The results showed that our approach achieved an average root mean square error of 1.7mm with respect to the target's position, outperforming traditional methods. This improvement was also evident when comparing our approach to a standard method that used optical flow for registration, especially when the image exposure angle varied. Our strategy was also tested with real-world clinical images, where it demonstrated similar levels of accuracy to the standard method.

Single-particle entanglement has long been regarded as an intriguing concept, yet it has largely been excluded from serious research into the fundamental aspects of quantum theory. To address this disregard, we present a revised GPS analogy that incorporates single-particle entanglement, and in doing so, we expose the limitations of the original analogy. Furthermore, we present evidence that single-particle entanglement is essential for accurately predicting the trajectory of a particle guided by its wave function, and that other variants of the analogy fail to capture this behavior.

The integration of federated learning into education delivered through intelligent transportation systems has gained significant attention lately, yet existing proposals fall short in addressing several crucial concerns. Several challenges persist in these proposals, including insecure update transmissions, unauthorized access, centralized management structures, and transparent transaction monitoring. To overcome these difficulties, researchers have started exploring collaborations between federated and blockchain technologies. However, current studies on this collaboration within the field of education delivered through intelligent transportation systems are limited due to the scarcity of comprehensive surveys on this topic. To rectify this gap, this paper meticulously examines and analyzes various federated learning approaches for enhancing privacy in education delivered through intelligent transportation systems, as well as potential blockchain technologies that can facilitate transparency in this framework. By doing so, this paper aims to guide future research directions at the concluding part of this study.

Astronomers observed that V392 Persei, a white dwarf star in a binary system, suddenly increased its \gamma-ray brightness due to a nova explosion on July 12, 2021, without prior signs of visible or other forms of electromagnetic radiation bursts. V392 Persei had been closely monitored for nearly three decades before this event, with data indicating the binary stars orbit each other every 3.4 days and there's an approaching eclipse that could have started as early as May 2021. Based on its system properties, V392 Persei was expected to experience a Type Ia supernova on the same timeline. The system's small nova radius suggests a low mass transfer rate, which does not fully explain the observed \gamma-ray brightness of the supernova-like outburst. The observed spectrum also revealed a complex structure, consisting of multiple zones, one excited by highly efficient electron scattering that may have been influenced by the passing eclipse. Estimates of the nova blast wave's energy indicate a highly effective process, with only 10 percent of the energy being radiated as observed radiation, which is lower than the typical 30 to 50 percent efficiency of many novae outbursts. V392 Persei will continue to be observed to provide more insights into this unusual event, especially during the upcoming days when more radiation will be observed as the eclipse begins in late August 2021.

To maintain fault tolerance beyond the bare error rate, it's necessary to perform operations on more than two qubits when using the toric code, whether through global interactions or local measurements combined with the code's weight-four syndrome extractions. In the process, we derive a general result for the threshold under these multi-qubit operations and investigate the interplay between global and local operations, which leads to a threshold around 0.01 for local interactions, comparable to the reported result of 0.007 for the surface code with 2D check operators as published in Nature Communications in 2019.

Limited backward link feedback size constrains the effectiveness of advanced transmission techniques in LTE and 5G systems. To address this challenge, we propose a refined feedback method that leverages Gaussian mixture models. This approach involves selecting a subset of precoders and power levels from predefined sets and choosing the best combination from all possibilities. The optimal set can even be pre-determined at the base station to minimize solution complexity. By testing this method on a point-to-point link, we found that it nearly matches the performance of optimal techniques, and when extended to multi-user scenarios, it outperforms existing feedback methods. Furthermore, simulations on 5G test beds demonstrate the proposed approach's potential for enhancing system performance with relatively low feedback overhead.

A 2D fluid confined within a periodically twisted 2-electron 1-hole universe exhibits rich, complex behavior, characterized by the Hofstadter mosaic, with multiple disjoint, isolated regions. We've developed a 3D version of this model and discovered that a fluid within it exhibits stable, chaotic nonequilibrium surface currents, appearing as thick, swirling ribbons. These ribbons correspond to 3D versions of the Hofstadter mosaic, with a detailed, intricate pattern. Notably, this stable, chaotic behavior is not restricted to idealized, isolated systems, as it persists when the 3D Hofstadter mosaic is slightly disturbed.

The Bondi mass loss theory is examined in relation to radiative outflows at the base of black hole disks, and a method is introduced to estimate the mass loss rate based on the radiative efficiency and the bondi mass loss rate. This estimation can be represented through a new parameter, the radiative pace of mass growth (RPMG). Radiative outflows that fully match the bondi mass loss rate are classified as radiatively effective, whereas those that fall short are considered radiatively ineffective. A statistical analysis was performed using a sample of 35 radio loud galaxies and active galactic nuclei, and the data revealed that radiatively ineffective black holes are more likely to be in a radio mode state. This relationship holds true for black holes under 10^8 solar masses and is supported by theoretical considerations. Furthermore, radiatively ineffective black holes are more likely to be associated with heavy disk states, and this connection is consistent with the stability of the viscous gravitational instability model.

We examine the possibility of gravitational waves reaching detectors from the first generations of massive stars in nuclear star clusters around supermassive black holes. Although previous studies suggest such stars would have been consumed very early, our analysis reveals they should still be present in small clusters today. These remaining stars may form binaries that emit detectable gravitational waves. Under specific conditions, there's a reasonable probability of finding these systems and they could contribute to the gravitational background affecting future gravitational wave observations. Our findings also highlight the need to observe the central regions of nearby galaxies more thoroughly.

The GECAM satellite, launched in December 2020 and consisting of two satellite units carrying 16 Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) detectors, is specifically designed to investigate GRBs and other high-energy phenomena. Unlike traditional methods, studying GRBs in China lacks physical models due to the high cost of actual GRB training. To address this, a mobile GRB simulator was created using Android technology and Java, which can digitally simulate a GRB event similar to what GECAM would detect. This prototype is intended for real-world testing with the GECAM ground station, and in this study, the design and evaluation of the simulator are presented, demonstrating its ability to accurately replicate key characteristics of GRB events, such as time-energy spectra and various timing parameters, when tested with simulated GECAM data.

We investigate the impact of several key factors on the stability of analytic function spaces under semigroups of composition operators and related integral operators. The spaces in question are denoted as $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{G})$ and their associated BMOA counterparts, $\mathcal{BMOA}(\mathcal{G})$, which are defined by certain admissible domains in the complex plane. Specifically, we look at a certain class of Dirac semigroups, known as the Komalov-Parrot semigroups, affecting functions within these spaces. Our study builds on previously established properties of the admissible domains, $\mathcal{G}$, to determine how the stability properties of $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{G})$ and $\mathcal{BMOA}(\mathcal{G})$ are influenced by the growth rate of the semigroup and its derivative, as well as by the boundary behavior of the mapping $\gamma_t$ generated by the semigroup. Notably, we establish a critical boundary between cases where the action of the semigroup is equivalent to a norm-preserving operation on the respective spaces, and cases where it results in an unbounded operation. These findings are then applied to identify sufficient conditions for the stability of the composition operator $C_{\phi_t}$ for all times, and characterize the subfamily of time-dependent symbol functions that ensure the stability of the composition operators within $\mathcal{B

It is widely accepted in the fields of physics and chemistry that a significant邓crepancy exists between the high rate of published papers and the actual growth of fundamental knowledge within these disciplines. To quantify the dissonance between productive output and the genuine expansion of knowledge, we propose a metric that compares the rate of published content with a model based on information theory. Our analysis, specifically focused on research outcomes in physics and chemistry from 1980 to 2019, reveals a significant divergence: while published content has increased at a rapid rate, the expansion of knowledge has modeled after slower, power-law growth patterns. The model's predictions concerning published content and knowledge are visually comparable but distinct when examined more closely. The slow growth of knowledge seems to be influenced by its restriction within an ever-narrowing conceptual framework, which can be characterized as an expanding volume in a vast space of possible ideas. The results suggest that the relationship between output and knowledge may be governed less by the quality of published content and more by a phenomenon known as the attention cycle, which suggests that a significant portion of the rapidly produced content receives limited engagement and ultimately gets overlooked.

In the context of dual-hop wireless networks with channel fading, we examined end-to-end performance in systems utilizing adaptive forwarding relays across multiple carriers. Prior research into these systems focused primarily on maximizing data transfer rates, giving little consideration to securing communication beyond rate optimization. To address this limitation, we proposed a novel application of multi-carrier technology that not only enhances data transfer rates but also provides novel insights into securing communication at both physical layers. We formulated a new optimization problem aimed at balancing achieving high data transfer rates and providing a robust level of security through careful allocation of power and bandwidth resources across multiple carriers. To solve this complex problem, we broke down the systems into two simpler sub-systems and employed an iterative algorithm to arrive at optimal resource allocation strategies. Our results indicate that in comparison to traditional single-carrier systems, these multi-carrier systems provide a significantly elevated level of security without sacrificing data transfer rates, thereby providing a more secure level of performance across a broader spectrum of scenarios.

Two-dimensional systems with robust, topologically non-trivial features contain defect-resistant edge currents, and under specific conditions, these systems generate localized modes at non-transmitting interfaces or impurities. This study utilizes quantum electrodynamic simulations to investigate the impact of these localized modes on light propagation along multi-channel waveguide edges. By applying experimental data and exploring various configurations of open and closed channels, including periodic arrangements with topologically distinct interior and exterior regions, complex scattering patterns are observed. Notably, certain configurations exhibit unaltered transmission regardless of closed channel arrangements, and in other cases, transmission increases with the addition of closed channels due to interference effects. Furthermore, we demonstrate control over transmission levels through the application of a global phase to light incident from specific channels.

Autonomous vehicles are expected to play a major role in the future of urban areas, and researchers are actively studying how these self-driving cars will interact with drivers who still operate their vehicles voluntarily. Our analysis focuses on a junction controlled by traffic signals, where self-driving cars coexist with regularly licensed drivers. We examine the complex, dynamic interactions between these two parties under traffic signal control and present a novel predictive management system for linked autonomous vehicles. This system anticipates future behavior, considers interactions with other vehicles and submits proposals for individual speed changes to optimize safety and efficiency. Our model incorporates potential collisions with other vehicles and drivers who operate their vehicles voluntarily, as well as upcoming traffic signal violations and provides robust proposal submissions using a method known as expectation propagation. We tested our model using real-world data and found that it can significantly reduce the frequency of collisions and improve overall safety and efficiency.

The advancements in mastering complex tasks using large language models have been significant. Researchers have developed models like ALPACAgent that combine these models with automated reasoning tools such as world models. As a benchmark, TextWorld has been established to assess the problem-solving skills of these LLM-based agents, although it has limitations due to its slow model inference speed. For many tasks, the typical LLM agent performance is below human levels, leading to a slow learning speed when using reinforcement learning. To overcome this limitation, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a highly optimized emulation engine for text-based games with significantly reduced latency. This new system achieves up to 100 times faster simulation than TextWorld by employing an optimized implementation of game mechanics. We have demonstrated that our system enables environment  rewards within 10 milliseconds. Through the use of custom training protocols for LR and RL, we have developed an agent that has reached a -0.55 expected reward within 3 hours of RL training. Notably, this is comparable to the original world-embracing agent performance but achieved in just 15 minutes of RL training. Furthermore, TextWorldExpress is available as an open-source platform for reinforcing learning with text-based games at significantly accelerated speeds.

Deep learning methods such as deep neural networks (DNNs) have excelled in complex tasks like video identification.
