determine star formation rates (SFRs) in regions where H$\alpha$ data is also
available. Br$\gamma$ is less affected by dust absorption, which improves
spatial resolution and reduces the need to correct for absorption during SFR
derivation. Comparing Br$\gamma$-based SFRs to H$\alpha$-based SFRs, derived
independently from single-template and multi-template spectral energy distribution (SED)
fits, we found that when resolving regions into small pixel grids, the
br$\gamma$ method underestimated SFRs by a factor of 10. However, when
combining Br$\gamma$ and H$\alpha$ flux, we found that it overestimated
SFRs by a factor of 3. When comparing Br$\gamma$ and H$\alpha$ flux directly,
we discovered an offset of 1.5 in log space and a magnitude offset of 0.5 in
magnitude space. When comparing Br$\gamma$ and H$\alpha$-based SFRs derived
from both single and multi-template SED fits, we found that the Br$\gamma$
method underestimated SFRs by a factor of 5 to 7. These outcomes are
inconsistent with each other and are primarily due to flux estimation
biases, which are affected by the resolution
We identify an extensive class of vertex locations within the interior of the nonnegative octant, yet adjacent to the boundary of the SOS cone's closure.

New high-precision measurements of neutrino oscillation patterns could potentially reveal that the neutrino mixing matrix isn't unitary, and researchers are currently analyzing the data that FASER$
u$ is expected to produce to test a specific theory called "leptonic non-unitarity". This theory suggests that the neutrino mixing matrix isn't unitary as a result of heavy new particles that communicate with standard model leptons. If the particles predicted by leptoquarks or $SO(10)$ see-saw mechanisms don't exist, then the neutrino mixing matrix would be found to be approximately unitary based on the data that FASER$
u$ could provide, and these measurements would contribute to the study of lepton flavor universality violation. On the other hand, the full non-unitarity space would be effectively probed for any of these scenarios through analyses of neutrino oscillations, charged current interactions, and coherent neutrino interactions. The results from these tests can also constrain the parameters of post-inflationary leptogenesis models, and researchers suggest that FASER$
u$ should also look for sterile neutrinos in the discharge of a beam dump. This search would involve analyzing long-distance $\mu^{\pm}$ spectra that are produced when a neutrino beam is produced. The constraints on these neutrino-related parameters would be significantly improved by a factor of up to 3-10 with the data that FASER$
u$ is expected to produce, and

Alphabet-based regular expressions with intersection and complement operations can effectively be utilized to represent and manipulate automata languages. This approach enables the development of a comprehensive and compact syntax for specifying language relationships among automata and provides a foundational basis for next-generation program analysis tools. This document details an algorithm that takes as input a set of regular expression inequalities (possibly including all basic operations) and produces a symbolic resolution consisting of an equivalent set of inequalities without complement, thereby facilitating the application of existing NFA-based verification algorithms. The performance of this algorithm is evaluated through an implemented proof-of-concept and the resulting outcomes are comparative.

Our research focuses on improving the Precision-Recall F1 score in the scene reconstruction task of the PolyVision challenge, where a self-driving car reconstructs its journey through a virtual environment. Our ensemble model incorporates an external memory attention module called PolyVision with External Memory Focus (EMA-VIO). This approach fuses inputs from two parallel vision encoder branches and a separate external attention module. The external attention module selectively retrieves relevant external memory inputs to enhance the main network's scene reconstruction capabilities. Equally important is the need for a meaningful external attention module design. Experimental results demonstrate the significance of both the external attention module and the fusion of knowledge from multiple data sources, compared to a baseline model. Our EMA-VIO model achieves an impressive PolyVision score of 69.77%, placing it second in the recent challenges, with detailed explanations and figures available on our project page.

We propose a novel class of Weyl semimetals in three dimensions with zero-energy eigenstates exhibiting fractional dimensionality, specifically $\sqrt{t}$, at the faces of the photonic structure. These characteristics set our proposed "square-root elevated-order" Weyl semimetals apart from conventional WYSMs or high-order Weyl points. Utilizing microwave resonators, we have experimentally confirmed the presence of zero-energy square-root Weyl points and related phenomena, such as the anomalous Hall effect and near-surface electron localization. The proposed mechanism for achieving zero-energy square-root Weyl points involves simultaneously breaking time-reversal, translational, and inversion symmetries, followed by adjusting system parameters to align the gapless modes. Our work opens up a new research direction in the study of exotic high-order Weyl phenomena.

This study focuses on resolving an incomplete boundary value issue related to the exterior source term of the first type for the time-dependent Maxwell equations. A quasi-reversible numerical approach is employed to solve this external boundary value problem, and its convergence properties are theoretically proven. Additionally, several computational methods utilizing finite differences, finite elements in space, and central differences in time are derived and analyzed.

This work introduces a parafermion vertex operator algebra associated with the Kac-Moody Lie algebra $osp(1|2n)$ at a specific level $k$. We establish its structure by determining its primary fields, descent constructs, and spiral elements, while also identifying it with the affine Lie algebra $sl(2n+2)$ at an equivalent, higher level in the Kac-Kazhdan series.

The federated learning technique has been successful in bringing
virtual learning on a large scale to many sectors. One significant issue
encountered is the disparity between various institutions' knowledge bases,
which hinders the synchronization of information. Through the application of
a federated discriminative aggregation method, the organization can overcome
this challenge by indirectly integrating its knowledge with that of other
entities. This method enables the entity to maintain control over its
knowledge base and prevent direct data exchange. Furthermore, it is possible
to incorporate the scale effect of federated training into this method, which
can further enhance its effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate the
efficacy of the proposed approach in terms of recall and F1-score in both
knowledge integration scenarios, yielding satisfactory outcomes.

The mammalian brain's navigation and spatial orientation capabilities are heavily dependent on entorhinal cortex grid cells. These unique neurons, found within the medial entorhinal cortex, fire in a pattern that forms a grid across a two-dimensional surface in response to an animal's movement through space. Research into grid cells is progressing rapidly due to their accessibility for study using non-invasive magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in humans, in addition to detailed neural examinations possible in laboratory animal models utilizing various types of stimuli in controlled environments. In this review, we examine current research on grid cell properties from behavioral experiments involving rodents and non-invasive human MRI studies, in an effort to establish a foundation for future investigations into the capabilities of entorhinal grid cell systems for spatial memory, map creation, and environmental modeling.

Hydrodynamic simulations of solar-like stars reveal a difference in rotation speeds between their poles and equator, inversely proportional to their distance from the pole. This differential rotation pattern can vary, and in some cases, contributes to the development of magnetic cycles through a dynamo process. This process is linked to the star's spin rate, and eventually, these stars stop rotating. This study explores how dynamic processes, specifically the star's spin rates and turbulent fluctuations, influence magnetic cycles in these solar-like stars. Results from this investigation show that differential rotation has influence on magnetic field fluctuations, while boundary conditions, which are affected by the star's spin rates, also contribute to field cycle characteristics. Notably, an end-state scenario emerges where magnetic cycles disappear due to changes in stability caused by the star's spin rates.

Using advanced computation and theoretical analysis, we examine the statistical patterns of elliptic curve rank within certain quartic field extensions belonging to the symmetry groups $A_4$ and $S_4$. Specifically, we focus on subsets of quartic fields that exhibit identical algebraic invariants but distinct ramification behaviors. To explore this, we analyze pairs of quartic fields for a variety of base elliptic curves, revealing an intriguing correlation between rank distribution and their A4 or S4 symmetry. Our findings suggest a correlation-driven effect on rank distribution within these quartic fields and may imply its connectivity to the modularity of associated L-functions. Moreover, we investigate the implications of our data for understanding rank rank conjectures.

Our research investigates quantum thermodynamics within the quench-time evolution of quench states, initiated by a sudden local perturbation within a relativistic field theory coupled to gravity. By analyzing its retarded correlator and quench-time paths, we found that the minimal energy quench time corresponds to a tractable spacetime geometry. This discovery is supported by multiple consistency checks and applies to states that are semiclassical in their gravitational duals. Specifically, we observed that the fidelity of these quench states near the minimal energy quench time can be calculated, and this is applied to and corroborated by field theoretic computations for multiple models. Furthermore, we established quantum inequalities of motion for the quench-time paths of arbitrary states, deriving exponential bounds on the expansion rates, and these are validated by multiple consistency checks. Additionally, we investigated how these quench dynamics are reflected in universal behaviors of minimal surfaces, including entangling surfaces whose expansion rates are limited by the QNEC, and these findings are supported by multiple aspects of the study.

Quantum velocity limits, also known as discriminability durations, serve as fundamental measures of the speed at which quantum states change. Various types of quantum velocity limits have been developed for different applications, and recently, the concept of discriminability durations in the context of Bloch spheres has been introduced as a fundamental limit for quantum state evolution. In this paper, we introduce discriminability velocities in more complex Hilbert spaces and demonstrate their role in capturing the essence of quantum velocity limits. Furthermore, we introduce a class of monotone functions that monotonically decrease under certain types of unitary transformations, and utilize these functions to derive a broader class of quantum velocity limits within the Bloch sphere. Finally, we introduce discriminability asymmetry monotones and demonstrate how they serve as discriminability velocities and can be employed to discriminate between different types of quantum evolution generators.

The paper establishes a specific inequality for the norm of an interpolation operator related to the second difference of a function in the $L^1$-norm. 
This inequality is derived from a previously proven result. 
Furthermore, the author obtains a particular bound for the norm of the interpolation operator based on the first difference of a function in the $L^1$-norm. 
Notably, this bound is in response to an unresolved query raised by Phuc, Van Diejen, and Zhou. 
Additionally, the results obtained within the framework of weighted spaces are also discussed.

We utilize terahertz nano-scopic imaging to investigate the electric field distributions within superconducting niobium resonators at various resonance frequencies. Our findings, when compared to theoretical calculations, reveal local hot-spots on the resonator surface, characterized by enhanced field intensities, that do not conform to the expected phase patterns. These defects, likely caused by fabrication errors and material inhomogeneities, have a significant impact on noise levels and may hinder the realization of multi-qubit quantum circuits.

This lecture will introduce basic concepts from algebraic $K$-theory and motivic homotopy theory, and explain how they connect. The relationship between these two fields was first established by Morel, who demonstrated that algebraic $K$-theory forms the universal Thom spectrum for a specific cohomology theory, leading to notable discoveries about the connective algebraic $K$-theory of a point and finite fields. The next generation of researchers then introduced the $\ku$ and $\bm{\mathbb{H}\mathbb{H}}$ spectra as representatives of these theoretical counterparts, and explored how other spectra can be understood through the lens of motivic homotopy theory. The final part of the lecture will introduce some recent findings that suggest enriching the motivic homotopy category with additional structure, and examine the far-reaching implications this has on algebraic $K$-theory and topological $J$-hometry.

The complex dynamics of atmospheric evolution on Earth and other planetary bodies are heavily influenced by various factors including changes in the composition of the atmosphere and crust, the rotation of the planet, and the output of its star. This intricate web of feedback mechanisms plays a crucial role in determining the long-term development of a planetary body's atmosphere. The theory of atmospheric evolution has made significant advancements in the past decade, with researchers utilizing computer models to simulate the evolution of different atmospheric compositions over extended periods. These computer models can provide a extended-term perspective on how a particular atmospheric composition would evolve, offering valuable insights into the formation of Earth's current atmosphere, the stagnant greenhouse atmosphere of Venus, and even potential future scenarios for Mars. In this paper, the principles of atmospheric computer modeling are outlined for different scenarios including Earth's atmosphere, Venus's atmosphere, and the potential formation of atmospheres on Mars and exoplanets. The paper also explores the concept of using atmospheric computer modeling to forecast the future trajectories of atmospheres, including continued heating of Venus's atmosphere, potential preservation of habitability on the Earth's atmosphere, and the formation of atmospheres on Mars and exoplanets.

Investigating ultrafast molecular dynamics within soft matter can be challenging with current characterization techniques and often requires techniques that perturb the system under study. To overcome these limitations, researchers used a novel method to examine ion emission from sub-wavelength glycol droplets, leveraging the resolution-enhancing capabilities of nanoscopy based on local field excitation. By comparing data from water and 1,2-propanediol droplets, they discovered that glycols exhibit significantly longer inter-hydrogen bond lifetimes despite similar hydrogen-bonding network properties. This difference was further supported by reaction-imaged absorption spectra and joint electronic-hydrogen bond maps, showing glycols have distinct electronic environments around their hydrogen-bond networks. These findings highlight the potential of nanoscopy in examining ultrafast molecular dynamics and could facilitate the exploration of similar phenomena in other multi-hydrogen atom-containing substances.

Migdal's recursion theorem enables the creation of Matrix Product State representations, which can be decomposed into simple quantum circuits at a given depth. Conversely, a basic quantum circuit can be easily converted into an MPSTwist representation through the application of the Schwinger-Zumel reciprocity theorem. However, directly using this theorem leads to highly complex gates within the circuit. By incorporating the Migdal's step with the Schwinger-Zumel reciprocity theorem, we can take a simple finite-depth circuit and expand it into an MPSTwist that still maintains this limited interaction property, provided the bond dimension is sufficiently high. This combined approach reveals that the capacity to create such limited-interaction MPSTwists abruptly drops at a specific threshold, analogous to the bond dimension phase transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate that through the combination of these techniques, we can also transform MPSTwists into equally complicated but structurally distinct low-depth circuits.

The creation of analytical tools for pathologists to study tissue samples has been on the forefront of research in digital pathology, with existing methods breaking down images into hierarchical grids and extracting features at each level. Although some researchers have focused on extracting features from individual cells or cell clusters, no study has explored a comprehensive, multi-level representation of images that captures both the arrangement of cells and clusters. In contrast, recent work on scene understanding in computer vision has developedHNR networks that generate multi-level representations by combining parts from lower levels and using extracted features as building blocks for higher levels. Building on theHNR architecture and incorporating attention mechanisms, a newly proposed model has been trained to accurately predict the presence of malignant cells in pathology images, with impressive results surpassing the best-pathologist performance. Furthermore, this model's attention maps were utilized to generate accurate and efficient descriptions of pathologists, with very high accuracy and minimal errors.

We present a non-linear version of the Reversible Hawkes process and utilize it to model and analyze the dynamics of cryptocurrency markets. By employing a specific non-linear model, we investigate and predict the sequence of blockchain transactions, demonstrating the utility of our approach through real-world data. Our study reveals a direct correlation between the inferred relationships between cryptocurrencies and their price correlation. Additionally, we observe distinct temporal patterns in the transaction data, characterized by short-term hyperactivity followed by intermediate stability and long-term reversibility.

This paper builds on our previous work in Reference 1, which introduced a novel numerical method known as the Rapid Multipole Technique (RMT) to resolve time-dependent problems involving particles moving under complex, changing forces. Building upon the success of the Rapid Multipole Technique, this research extends its application to account for particles' rotational movements caused by varying force fields. By incorporating the preservation of angular momentum, this study enables more accurate simulation of particle dynamics and provides a deeper understanding of their interactions. Furthermore, this work introduces updated formulations and algorithms within the RMT framework, specifically designed to capture preissager effects and rapidly compute torque during particle rotations. These advancements are supported by detailed mathematical derivations and demonstrated effective results through numerical experiments.

Successfully adapting segmentation models to new domains is crucial for advancing the field of medical image analysis.  While domain adaptation techniques have shown promise, the target domain still plays a significant role in the final results.  In this study, we observed that certain target domains are easier to adjust to than others, and identified a key characteristic that distinguishes them: the educational background of the images.  Images from domains with the same general anatomical category but different sub-specialties are said to have the same 'educational background.'  We defined a new strategy called Comparative Specialized Education (CSE) to capture this difference.  Within CSE, transferable task-specific knowledge acts as a contrast between domains, and more significant differences lead to stronger contrast.  This concept is reflected in our Comprehensive CSE Loss function.  Experimental results demonstrate that CSE enhances the domain alignment process, resulting in significant improvements in segmentation accuracy across multiple datasets, outperforming strong competitive methods.  The code is openly available at https://github.com/QijunWan/Contrastive-Semi-Supervised-Medical-Image-Segmentation.

The success of the 1.5 order framework in gauge theory has been examined, but its application to gravity or supergravity has produced inconsistent results. A rigorous test revealed that the 1.5 order formalism fails to yield a legitimate Brustein-Roiban-Siegel (BRS) transformation for supergravity, thereby demonstrating its limitations in this context. Furthermore, an alternative approach based on the count of degrees of freedom has been explored, but it arrived at a conflicting conclusion.

The polarization of high-power laser pulses is typically reduced upon interacting with a plasma, especially at multi-petawatt levels, inhibiting certain applications. We demonstrate a novel, efficient method to increase and alter laser polarization by incorporating a twisted magnetic field into the plasma, even with high-power pulses. Our method所涉及的结构只需简单的修正,  可将 linear polarization enhancement by a factor of 14 achieve, the maximum value of  1.09 times  original polarization found,  并使用两组正交圆形的等离子体结构,  可将 polarization提升 ten  times  or more,  即使对于 multi-petawatt levels  亦然.  这些发现  指示我们的 method  可有效提升  和 alter  高-power lasers  的 polarization  within  等离子体 media,  可有效 support  未来激光等离子体 applications, such as  有效 drive  新型 high-power laser  等离子体 accelerators,  增强  放射性同位素  生产,  和  改进  某些  激光等离子体  加速器的  辐射源.

Using latest data from the Belle experiment, the shape of the tau lepton's differential angular distribution is determined across a wide range of energies. The findings indicate a differential electric dipole distribution parameter of 0.049 ± 0.014, which represents the most precise measurement of this parameter to date. Additionally, the study establishes upper limits of 0.014 and 0.028 (95% confidence level) for the tau's color dipole and axial color dipole moments. These constraints are significantly more precise than previous limits set by experiments at LEP and hadron colliders.

Computerized memory systems, utilized for storing information, have the capability to track two types of errors in data, namely bit errors and rank errors. The former occur when a single bit is incorrectly measured, while the latter happen when an entire memory bank, or rank, yields incorrect readout. To address these errors, modern memory controllers have the ability to combine both types of measurements into a unified error signal. This study investigates the potential of correcting up to three rank errors by leveraging this combined error signal, a capability that current systems have yet to fully exploit. Moreover, we explore a new coding scheme that can achieve this correction capability and demonstrate its effectiveness through a performance assessment.

In the context of AdS/CFT, conformal blocks representing three-point operator interactions are utilized to analyze more intricate correlation functions. In AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$, considering only the symmetry group, there's a limited set of such blocks up to a specific transformation. This paper extends a previous study by incorporating additional considerations, namely spin-carrying external operators and potential terms into the analysis, to derive explicit recursive formulas for bootstrap calculations. Furthermore, it provides closed-form expressions for even-spin cases and demonstrates how these results decompose into constituent exchange operators within the shadow operator formalism.

Future experiments to study the Cosmic Microwave Background will be able to measure a extremely small signal from scalar-mode inflationary disturbances on a precise scale, however current forecast predictions based on traditional analysis techniques fall short of what is actually achievable. By utilizing specialized techniques and taking advantage of information from multiple frequency bands and high-resolution observations, machine learning methods can be used to more efficiently extract information from the MICA and E-ASTROSCOPE mission areas, allowing for a more accurate measurement of the signal from scalar-mode disturbances.

Gelfand and MacPherson's 1962 geometric approach to defining Pontrjagin classes is reviewed. A key aspect of their method involved constructing a stratified space from the power bundle over a given manifold, and this construction will be completed by incorporating the missing boundary strata. The revised construction yields a well-defined cobordism module associated with the power bundle, and this module is shown to be isomorphic to the traditional polynomial structure via homological methods.

We analyzed SN~2020jfo, a Type II-S supernova with a short plateau, using both ground-based observations from 2020 and 2021, as well as data from the TESS space telescope. The light curves derived from the visible and infrared spectra showed a typical plateau duration of around 15-16 days, and the spectral analysis with the NIRES spectrograph revealed persistent H-alpha emission 42 days after the explosion. Additionally, we determined an absolute magnitude of -14.3 and a 56Fe mass of approximately $2\times 10^{-4}M_{\odot}$ from the optical and NIR spectra. The energy derived from the optical spectra was initially super-Maxwellian but became sub-Maxwellian with time. The slope of the energy derived from the NIR spectra mirrored that of the SN Ia equivalent data, indicating a more complex process than a simple energy balance. Furthermore, we found an expanding photosphere with velocities of around 10,000 km/s in both the optical and NIR spectra. The mass of the ejected material was around 5.3$M_{\odot}$ from the optical spectra and between 3.6 and 12.5$M_{\odot}$ from the NIR spectra. Finally, the derived masses of hydrogen and electrons were consistent with those obtained from the energy and momentum equations, supporting the validity of our

We analyze striped lobster-eye lens arrays for X-ray imaging, considering their unique ability to capture and reflect X-rays.  The performance of these lenses is limited by their surface reflection, specifically the edges of the lens structures.  Using a geometric optics model, we determine that these lenses can still effectively image sources, despite having low efficiency due to the absorption and reflection of X-rays.  The resolution of the lens depends on its geometry and the energy of the X-rays, but the flat edges of the lens structures cause a problem with the uniformity of the resolution across the lens.  A potential solution to this issue is explored, along with a calculation of the lens' efficiency and resolution through simulation.  The analysis indicates that the lens can have an overall effective resolution of around 2-3 mm at 3 keV, with approximately 10% of incident X-rays reaching the detector.  The design has implications for a broad class of flat-panel detectors, enabling them to effectively measure the intensity of the imaged X-ray source.

We establish a stage-set version of partial uniform ellipticity and associated results, including Degenerate Besov space bounds and a stochastically continuous modulus of continuity, as expected outcomes. These achievements are made possible by introducing a stage-set framework for differential operators. Specifically, we derive the stage-set uniform ellipticity condition and prove that it ensures the stage-set degenerate Besov space and Holder space regularity for elliptic and parabolic equations involving second-order differential operators. Current proofs rely on technical assumptions about coefficient behavior, which we show can be derived from the stage-set parabolic uniform ellipticity condition.

A new hypothesis suggesting that dark matter's properties, not its amount, dictate the cosmos' structure has long been explored. In this research, a specialized technique inspired by the physics of Lagrangian trajectories is applied to investigate the influence of the cosmic velocity field on the formation of galaxies and clusters. A groundbreaking discovery using this approach is that certain properties of the velocity distribution within dark matter halos consistently hold true across a range of densities and universally apply to various types of galaxy clusters. Additionally, research comparing models with varying amounts of dark matter and the proposed model of the speed field has largely been conducted, with inconclusive results. Given these findings, a necessary exploration now lies ahead - investigating if this proposed model of the cosmos' structure formed through the influence of the velocity distribution accurately mirrors the actual formation process of the universe.

Ai-NOTE is a state-of-the-art music transcription system that utilizes Convolutive Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (CNMF) to achieve high accuracy in semi-supervised transcription. CNMF excels at modeling the blurred spectral patterns characteristic of music recordings. Leveraging the powerful Semi-Supervised Convolutive NMF (SCCNMF) variant, which extends the basics of CNMF, allows for even better performance. However, applying CNMF in a music transcription task proves to be a challenging task. This is where the SCCNMF variant shines, facilitating faster and more stable optimization through the use of conjugate gradient methods. By employing the SCCNMF framework, the SCCNMF algorithm enhances the semi-supervised transcription accuracy of convolutive models. The authors extend the SCCNMF framework to accommodate mono-instrument music transcription, and introduce the Ai-NOTE 2.0 system, which features the SCCNMF as one of its components. The new system demonstrates significant improvements in transcription fidelity when compared to its predecessor and other leading music transcription systems. The system outperforms its competitors in multiple evaluation datasets, achieving the highest scores in weighted F1 and edit distance metrics.

A new, comprehensive approach is presented for computing rotating stars in the context of general relativity. This method develops solutions incrementally from slowly to rapidly spinning stars through iterative, non-linear calculations. By demonstrating key concepts and achieving both slow and fast rotating solutions, the approach has been successfully validated. Furthermore, initial results have been established for realistic astrophysical scenarios and have revealed distinct characteristics in fluid flow patterns distinguishing slow from fast rotating stars.

A AI-driven solution for analyzing complex reports and forms is an essential component of the knowledge graph construction process. One critical framework step involves using visually-based AI to extract information from large collections of visually rich documents. To achieve this, numerous methods have been tried and failed, but none have proven effective in practice. These methods are typically evaluated through visual AI competitions, yet they are slow, costly, and require significant human input to label large numbers of images. This paper proposes a groundbreaking approach that significantly reduces the expense of creating labels for images by leveraging advanced machine learning techniques. The method, called Search-Assisted Dual-Process Learning (SADPL), allows for the evaluation of visual AI frameworks for large-scale search-based document review projects, and achieves remarkable results in terms of both expense and accuracy when compared to current methods. The evaluation of 9 leading visual AI frameworks using SADPL produced highly consistent, reliable outcomes, surpassing expectations in terms of expense, accuracy, and usability.

The merger of a Neutron Star and a Black Hole produces a variety of gravitational wave signatures that depend on the mass ratio of the two objects, the spin of the Neutron Star, and the quality of its surface.  By analyzing the gravitational wave signal, we can obtain insight into the behavior of matter under extreme conditions, the nature of any electromagnetic radiation emitted, and the characteristics of the merger itself.  To explore the possibilities of detecting Ns-BH mergers, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of a large set of gravitational wave signals based on numerical relativity simulations, taking into account multiple variables including the mass of the objects involved, the spin of the Black Hole, and the properties of the Neutron Star.  Using the evaluated set of waveforms, we developed a deep learning approach to identify and classify Ns-BH mergers, achieving a minimum classification accuracy of 71% with a training time of 71 seconds per epoch and a inference time of 49 seconds per evaluation, outperforming similar approaches for detecting these types of mergers.  Furthermore, our results indicate that the success of this process is influenced by the degree of overlap between the gravitational wave signals produced by Ns-BH mergers and those generated by binary neutron star or binary black hole mergers.  While the current results are not yet sensitive to all possible Ns-BH merger cases, they do demonstrate the possibility of identifying these events with LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA III

The availability of online personal information and online discussions poses a significant challenge, as it is often used to predict an individual's health conditions. The task of discovering the connection between social information and healthcare conditions is complicated due to the need to automatically identify social aspects, such as emotions and personality traits, that are relevant to a person's health. In this paper, we explore a novel connection between social aspects and healthcare conditions and present a new token-based neural network model to accurately capture the relevant elements. Our approach also involves a unique technique for efficiently selecting emotion and personality tags from extensive label sets, which is then applied to a diverse set of online forum users across multiple classification targets. Experimentation on real-world data demonstrates the model's ability to achieve high accuracy in predicting individuals' conditions, as well as providing valuable insights into the relationship between social factors and healthcare conditions. Furthermore, our results highlight the importance of accurately identifying the relevant social aspects for this prediction task.

This paper delves into a more comprehensive understanding of optimal control through several "scallop theorem" scenarios. It demonstrates the utility of phase space visualizations, particularly in grasping the overall structure of a system and utilizing invariant manifolds for solution reduction. Additionally, it highlights the concept of value function gluing and its implications on reducing the dimensionality of the costate in systems with reduced freedom in their control inputs.

Researchers studied urban mobility and social interaction patterns to better understand the spread dynamics of contagious diseases. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the purpose of studying urban mobility and social interaction patterns changed, with municipalities trying to discourage unnecessary meetings and promote social distancing. A new method was developed to analyze the nature of social interactions in the context of pandemic spread, withP-entropy being introduced to differentiate between contacts made for essential activities, such as working from home or visiting grocery stores, and those made for non-essential activities. A data set was used to track changes in mobility and social interactions over time in nine US urban areas. Analysis revealed that the nature of social interactions underwent significant changes, with home-based activities increasing and work-related interactions declining. Research indicated that these changes in social interactions played a critical role in interrupting pandemic transmission more so than mere changes in mobility. A surprising effect was also observed in urban areas with high proportion of remote workers. There, even with little change in overall mobility, the nature of social interactions switched completely, with increases inP-entropy corresponding to decreases in expected metapopulation reproduction ratio. According to this effect, urban areas with high proportion of remote workers experienced amplified declines in infection rates compared to areas with little change in these interactions' nature. Furthermore, expected metapopulation reproduction ratio was found directly related to expected individual-level entropy of daily visits to various destinations. According to this relationship, infection spread was most effective in situations where people visited the same places daily.

Observations of young stellar objects suggest a significant correlation between high-mass accretion periods and the formation of nearby dense gas structures through accretion disk precession, which may also influence jet outflows. To better understand massive star formation, we conducted high-resolution, global hydrodynamic simulations of three massive protostars with 15, 25, and 40 solar masses, respectively. These simulations incorporated accurate treatment of radiative transfer, accurate phase transitions, and two-fluid dynamics to better model the process of mass accumulation and mergers with adjacent gas structures. Our findings indicate that massive star formation is episodic and closely tied to the formation of neighboring gas structures, with quiescent periods characterized by outflows that are driven by jet outflows and quenching of adjacent structures, often resulting in mergers that lead to more intense periods of mass accumulation. The relationship between active mass accumulation and outflows supports the hypothesis that massive star formation may continue to be influenced by feedback mechanisms, including those proposed by the light radiative feedback and accretion-shock precession models. Furthermore, our data suggest that turbulent fragmentation within massive protoplanetary disks could contribute to angular momentum transport that facilitates efficient mass accumulation.

To tackle the challenge of constructing algebraic quantum field theories, we employ a method of decomposing the algebras of observables into wedges and circles using spatial slices. This approach enables us to systematically analyze the relationships between smaller components and the algebras of observables. Within the framework of local QFT, we prove the existence of a bipartite net, initially established in E. Valerio, A. Sorella, S. Theisen, S. Trevisan, we then extend this research to the setting of free scalar fields, providing a concrete example through scattering theory. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our constructions accurately reflect the structural properties of the bipartite model, we demonstrate in a bipartite DHR category, first explored in S. Theisen, S. Trevisan, that for free scalar fields, there exists a unitary equivalence, we establish that the data of scattering theory accurately captures the essential characteristics of the theory, providing a macroscopic perspective.

The rapid expansion of 5G networks is being accelerated, and with higher adoption rates expected, it is crucial to examine the levels of radio wave exposure from these mast facilities. Specifically, research needs to be conducted on the typical 5G mast infrastructure to determine how much emitted radiation children and teenagers are typically exposed to in various settings, including schools and medical facilities. This study is focused on investigating the typical emission levels from 5G mast facilities and assessing the typical exposure children and teenagers experience in these environments. Furthermore, the research is updated with recent 5G frequency advancements.

We have developed a Hamiltonian Dysthe approximation for deep-water gravity waves, where the water's surface vorticity is uniform. This model is derived using a Dysthe expansion technique and shares similar characteristics with the original Dysthe equation, particularly in its conservation properties. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that under specific conditions, our Hamiltonian Dysthe model converges to the Euler equations that describe gravity waves with uniform vorticity, under appropriate topological constraints.

We introduce a novel differential structure known as locally arching rings and spaces, which we believe offers a robust framework for algebraic geometry. These constructions are named for their inherent "arching" property, which implies the existence of unique differential operators and locally definable parameters. We prove a local Stokes theorem for locally arching rings, which implies a version of the change of variables rule for integrals over arching rings. This result may potentially provide an algebraic foundation for integrals over manifolds.

This research paper presents a new control strategy for drones in multiple layers of space, using sonar sensors. By applying control techniques from robotics to the sonar's limited field of view, the team develops a method to use the data from sonar sensors more efficiently. They demonstrate that this approach allows for stable navigation and precise positioning even when working within the constraints of the sonar's field of view. Additionally, the team uses a simplifying assumption about angular acceleration to make real-time implementation possible on a drone.

False news that mimics real news and exploits people's fears has become increasingly difficult to distinguish from genuine news on social media. Current methods for detecting false news primarily focus on analyzing individual articles, often overlooking the diverse perspectives presented by credible sources. In contrast, our research considers multiple reports from established outlets when assessing the authenticity of a news article. We leverage text summarization techniques to automatically generate concise summaries of genuine and false news articles. Our experiments demonstrate that these generated summaries effectively facilitate the distinction between false news and real news. Additionally, they outperform several models utilizing only the original full-text articles.

The dynamic correlation of random fields as a function of spatial distance and the implications of embedding geometry are investigated using geodesic correlation functions and spectra of randomly distributed Gaussian fields on various surfaces. Correlation metrics are introduced specifically for stochastic surfaces and applied to evaluate the geometry's influence on correlations. Notably, the mean curvature of closed surfaces has a significant effect on the pair correlation and the power spectrum of randomly distributed two-dimensional surfaces.

We develop a gradient-based algorithm to efficiently calculate the principal component of a rotationally symmetric $\ell_1$-norm covariance matrix, using the property of symmetry to simplify the problem to a two-norm problem. This approach yields a closed-form expression for the second derivative of the objective function, which we leverage to modify the objective function for faster convergence. The proposed proximal gradient method converges linearly, a rare achievement for $\ell_1$-norm covariance matrix problems, and offers advantages over existing iterative methods especially when dealing with large datasets. Additionally, our algorithm demonstrates potential for calculating higher-order covariance matrix norms.

The emnlg task requires generating multi-word expressions to label the intended emotion of a single word within a sentence. To improve the efficiency of human review, a semantic tagging method has been proposed to group similar samples by their labels. However, the current approach faces a challenge: providing appropriate tags for words that are not encountered frequently. In this study, we introduce a semantic-supervised tagging method based on BERT to automate the process for novel words. The method involves generating multiple potential tags for unknown words by leveraging their contextual information and selecting the one that maximizes the confidence of a frequency-based classifier. We integrate this method with the original semantic tagging process and significantly boost its performance on emnlg datasets for under-sampled labels. The study examines power relations in completely ordered groups using a formal model.
This model is applied to understand dynamics within organizations, particularly in determining who has the most significant overall impact.
Key concepts, such as local and global power in directed graphs, are explored through this framework, specifically in the context of influence networks.
A new, comprehensive order-type based representation for finite power systems is developed, along with an examination of basic parameters like monotonicity.
Additionally, the study investigates the complexity of identifying global power structures, demonstrating that this task is inherently difficult (co-NP-complete) in general ordered groups but solvable in specific cases, particularly within the real numbers.

As wind accretion systems are renowned for their extreme ultraviolet and X-ray outputs, many researchers believe these features play a significant role in regulating the magnetic stars' magnetic fields. However, comparing UChMs and non-synchronous X-ray binaries poses challenges due to differences in stellar masses, ages, and potential evolutionary connections. Consequently, direct comparisons are unproductive. Instead, normalizing X-ray luminosity by the accretion disk's extreme ultraviolet luminosity, a parameter known as the torus ratio, effectively neutralizes several factors influencing X-ray emission, making it a valuable tool for studying accretion processes. When examining this torus ratio, distinct patterns emerge between asynchronous and non-synchronous systems, with former displaying a factor of ten range and latter displaying a factor of 100 range. Although further research is necessary to understand the exact normalization required for system synchronicity, this discovery highlights the importance of extreme ultraviolet and X-ray interactions in determining non-synchronous systems.

In this introductory chapter, we provide an overview of the Reduced Basis (RB) techniques applicable to both singular and multi-component fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problems. The principles and methods discussed will subsequently be utilized to establish the framework for the courses presented in Parts II to V of this series.

For robots to navigate independently, they need an effective diagram-based representation of environments that captures the spatial layout and object connections. Current representation systems, though capable, often result in complex structures that are hard to interpret, particularly in complex environments. In this paper, we propose a novel hierarchical topological diagram (HiTMap) representation, designed to simplify the structure by organizing subsets of elements into a tree-hierarchy. Each component in the HiTMap corresponds to a physical object or location, with connections representing their spatial relationships. We evaluate the HiTMap's performance in various tests, demonstrating its efficiency and ease of interpretation, particularly in complex environments.

This paper outlines our approach and outcomes for Task 1 of the SemEval-2019 Challenge on Detecting Offensive Language in Tweets. We participated in this challenge from the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Iowa State University, representing the LING group. Our objective was to classify tweets as offensive, not-defensive, or vitriolic based on input tweets. For evaluation, we used a comprehensive dataset consisting of 20,000 test tweets, the details of which have not been provided. We employed two separate models, an SVM and a BERT, to evaluate our approaches. Our BERT model achieved the highest accuracy of 76.40%, ranking second among 57 competing teams.

One of the most remarkable properties of atoms is their extraordinary sensitivity to external magnetic fields, which can be leveraged for precise measurement of locally altered magnetic fields. Traditional methods, like magnetometry, are limited to measuring fields on an atomic scale near the surface. In this research, we propose a novel approach to atom-based interferometry that takes advantage of the Meissner effect in superconductors to intermediate range attraction or repulsion between atoms, allowing for sensitive measurement of locally altered magnetic fields over longer distances. By using a superconducting slab as a source of attraction/repulsion and employing the interference of two matter-waves that experience opposite field shifts, we can achieve highly precise measurement of these alterations. The proposed method is so sensitive that it can potentially satisfy the end-to-end sensitivity requirement for detecting dark matter axion couplings.

The distinctive properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials have sparked interest in developing them into novel van der Waals heterostructures, which comprise multiple 2D layers held together by weak interlayer forces. Such structures often exhibit exotic physical properties not seen in their isolated 2D counterparts, including novel magnetic phenomena. A significant obstacle to studying and utilizing magnetism within these heterostructures is that ferromagnetic interactions typically diminish with added 2D layers. Contrary to this norm, we demonstrate the emergence of massive spin-polarized magnetocaloric effects (SMCEs) in an MoTe$_2$ monolayer when it is part of an MoIrTe$_4$ heterostructure. Through first-principles calculations, we observe large SMCEs spanning a broad temperature range activated by the spin-orbit coupling and interlayer interactions. The magnitude of SMCEs in these heterostructures far surpasses that of existing magnetocaloric materials and is tunable through variations in temperature, heterostructure composition, and light exposure, offering a superior platform for ultra-low-power, high-frequency, and gigahertz-scale thermal switching technologies.

This study investigates the impact of electron outflow and nonlocality on gap-plasmons in a bimetallic nanostructure as the gap size approaches zero. We examined how the electron outflow and nonlocality influences the gap-plasmons and derived a bivariate dispersion equation. Numerical results indicate that electron outflow and nonlocality has a significant impact on the gap-plasmons and the impact is most pronounced for larger velocity ratios and shorter screening lengths in the limit of vanishing intervals. A competing mechanism arises from the outflow that influences the impact of nonlocality. Moreover, the electron outflow and nonlocality's significance is highlighted by comparing it to the local model, which predicts an unrealistic, excessive impact on the decay of the electric field perpendicular to the interface as the gap decreases.
